23: #define MB_PHY_CMD_CHNL		(MAILBOX_BOX0)
24: #define MB_PHY_ACK_CHNL		(MAILBOX_BOX1)
25: 
26: #define CHNL_STATE_BUSY		1
27: #define CHNL_STATE_IDLE		0
28: 
29: /* If a physical channel stays BUSY longer than this (in milliseconds)
30:  * without seeing the matching ACK from the peer CPU, mb_chnl_write() will
31:  * forcibly recover it. Normal mailbox round-trips are << 1 ms, so 200 ms
32:  * is well clear of any legitimate burst while still keeping the system
33:  * responsive in the unlikely event the peer never replies. */
34: #define MB_PHY_CHNL_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS		200
35: 
36: typedef struct
37: {
38: 	volatile u8		tx_state;	/* physical channel tx state. */
39: 	u8		tx_seq;				/* physical channel tx sequence. */
40: 	u8		tx_log_chnl;		/* logical channel. */ /* bit7~bit4: dst/src CPU_ID, bit3~bit0: log_chnl_idx. */
41: 	u8		tx_hdr_cmd;
42: 	u32		rx_fault_cnt;
43: 	u32		tx_fault_cnt;
44: 
45: 	u32		param1;
46: 	u32		param2;
47: 	u32		param3;
48: 	/* Wall-clock (ms via rtos_get_time()) at which tx_state was set to
49: 	 * CHNL_STATE_BUSY. Used by mb_chnl_write() to detect a physical
50: 	 * channel that has been BUSY abnormally long (peer lost / dropped
51: 	 * the ACK) and forcibly clear it. 0 means "channel is IDLE". */
52: 	volatile u32	busy_since_ms;
53: } mb_phy_chnl_cb_t;
54: 
55: 
56: #define CHNL_CTRL_MASK			0xF
57: /*
58:  *  there are 2 boxes in one MAILBOXn HW,
59:  *  but no way to know which box this msg is from in current mailbox_driver design.
60:  *  use the CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX bit in the msg hdr.ctrl to distinguish where it is from.
61:  *  when CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX is set, it means from ack box ( MAILBOXn_BOX1 ).
62:  */
63: #define CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX		0x01
64: 
65: #define CHNL_CTRL_SYNC_TX		0x02
66: #define CHNL_CTRL_RESET			0x04
67: 
68: typedef union
69: {
70: 	struct
71: 	{
72: 		u32		cmd            : 8;
73: 		u32		state          : 4;
74: 		u32		ctrl           : 4;
75: 		u32		tx_seq         : 8;
76: 		u32		logical_chnl   : 8;
77: 	} ;
78: 	u32		data;
79: } phy_chnnl_hdr_t;
80: 
81: typedef struct
82: {
83: 	phy_chnnl_hdr_t	hdr;
84: 
85: 	u32		param1;
86: 	u32		param2;
87: 	u32		param3;
88: } mb_phy_chnl_cmd_t;
89: 
90: typedef struct
91: {
92: 	phy_chnnl_hdr_t	hdr;
93: 
94: 	u32		data1;
95: 	u32		data2;
96: 	u32		data3;
97: } mb_phy_chnl_ack_t;
98: 
99: typedef union
100: {
101: 	phy_chnnl_hdr_t		phy_ch_hdr;
102: 	mb_phy_chnl_cmd_t	phy_ch_cmd;
103: 	mb_phy_chnl_ack_t	phy_ch_ack;
104: 	mailbox_data_t		mb_data;
105: } mb_phy_chnl_union_t;
106: 
107: typedef struct
108: {
109: 	volatile u8		tx_state;				/* logical channel tx state. */
110: 	u8				in_used;
111: 	chnl_rx_isr_t		rx_isr;
112: 	chnl_tx_isr_t		tx_isr;
113: 	chnl_tx_cmpl_isr_t	tx_cmpl_isr;
114: 	void *				isr_param;
115: 	mailbox_data_t		chnnl_tx_buff;		/* logical channel tx buffer. */
116: } mb_log_chnl_cb_t;
117: 
118: #define PHY_CHNL_NUM		SYSTEM_CPU_NUM
119: 
120: static mb_phy_chnl_cb_t		phy_chnl_x_cb[PHY_CHNL_NUM];
121: static mb_log_chnl_cb_t		log_chnl_cb0[CP0_MB_LOG_CHNL_END - CP0_MB_LOG_CHNL_START];
122: static mb_log_chnl_cb_t		log_chnl_cb1[CP1_MB_LOG_CHNL_END - CP1_MB_LOG_CHNL_START];
123: #if PHY_CHNL_NUM > 2
124: static mb_log_chnl_cb_t		log_chnl_cb2[CP2_MB_LOG_CHNL_END - CP2_MB_LOG_CHNL_START];
125: #endif
126: #if PHY_CHNL_NUM > 3
127: static mb_log_chnl_cb_t		log_chnl_cb3[CP3_MB_LOG_CHNL_END - CP3_MB_LOG_CHNL_START];
128: #endif
129: 
130: static const u8 	phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[PHY_CHNL_NUM] = { 
131: 	ARRAY_SIZE(log_chnl_cb0),
132: 	ARRAY_SIZE(log_chnl_cb1),
133: #if PHY_CHNL_NUM > 2
134: 	ARRAY_SIZE(log_chnl_cb2),
135: #endif
136: #if PHY_CHNL_NUM > 3
137: 	ARRAY_SIZE(log_chnl_cb3),
138: #endif
139: //	CP0_MB_LOG_CHNL_END - CP0_MB_LOG_CHNL_START, 
140: 	};

143: 	&log_chnl_cb0[0], 
144: 	&log_chnl_cb1[0], 
145: #if PHY_CHNL_NUM > 2
146: 	&log_chnl_cb2[0], 
147: #endif
148: #if PHY_CHNL_NUM > 3
149: 	&log_chnl_cb3[0],

160: {

165: #endif // CONFIG_SOC_SMP

174: #endif // CONFIG_SOC_SMP
175: 
176: 	rtos_enable_int(flags);

182: static volatile uint32_t s_mailbox_rx_cnt = 0;
183: static volatile uint32_t s_mailbox_rx_ack_cnt = 0;
184: static volatile uint32_t s_mailbox_tx_ack_cnt = 0;
185: static volatile uint32_t s_mailbox_tx_compl_cnt = 0;
186: static volatile uint32_t s_mailbox_tx_ack_fault_mask = 0;

188: static inline bk_err_t bk_mailbox_send_safe(mailbox_data_t *data, mailbox_endpoint_t src, mailbox_endpoint_t dst, void *arg)
189: {
190: 	bk_err_t		ret_code;
191: 	
192: 	u32 int_mask = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
193: 	ret_code = bk_mailbox_send(data, src, dst, arg);
194: 	mb_chnl_exit_critical(int_mask);
195: 	
196: 	return ret_code;
197: }
198: 
199: 
200: static u8 mb_phy_chnl_tx_cmd(u8 log_chnl)
201: {
202: 	mb_phy_chnl_cmd_t	* cmd_ptr;
203: 	bk_err_t		ret_code;
204: 	u16 			chnl_type;
205: 	u8				phy_chnl_idx = GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl);   // = DST_CPU_ID;
206: 	u8				log_chnl_idx = GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(log_chnl);
207: 
208: 	mb_phy_chnl_cb_t * phy_chnl_ptr;
209: 	mb_log_chnl_cb_t * log_chnl_cb_x;
210: 
211: #if !CONFIG_SOC_SMP
212: 	/* for SMP project, log_chnl is always built by CPU0. it is always failed when call this API in CPU1. */
213: 	if(SELF_CPU != GET_SRC_CPU_ID(log_chnl))
214: 		return 4;
215: #endif
216: 
217: 	if(SELF_CPU == phy_chnl_idx)  // transferred to self.
218: 		return 5;
219: 
220: 	if(phy_chnl_idx >= PHY_CHNL_NUM)
221: 		return 3;
222: 
223: 	phy_chnl_ptr = &phy_chnl_x_cb[phy_chnl_idx];
224: 	log_chnl_cb_x = (mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)(phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[phy_chnl_idx]);
225: 
226: 	if(log_chnl_idx >= phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx])
227: 		return 1;
228: 
229: 	phy_chnl_ptr->tx_seq++;
230: 	phy_chnl_ptr->tx_log_chnl = log_chnl;
231: 
232: 	cmd_ptr = (mb_phy_chnl_cmd_t *)&log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].chnnl_tx_buff;
233: 
234: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl = log_chnl;
235: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.tx_seq = phy_chnl_ptr->tx_seq;
236: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.ctrl  = 0;
237: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.state = 0;
238: 
239: 	phy_chnl_ptr->tx_hdr_cmd = cmd_ptr->hdr.cmd;
240: 
241: 	phy_chnl_ptr->param1 = cmd_ptr->param1;
242: 	phy_chnl_ptr->param2 = cmd_ptr->param2;
243: 	phy_chnl_ptr->param3 = cmd_ptr->param3;
244: 
245: 	__DMB();
246: 	chnl_type = MB_PHY_CMD_CHNL;
247: 
248: 	mailbox_endpoint_t    dst_cpu = (mailbox_endpoint_t)(phy_chnl_idx);
249: 
250: 	ret_code = bk_mailbox_send(&log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].chnnl_tx_buff, SELF_CPU, dst_cpu, (void *)&chnl_type);
251: 
252: 	if(ret_code != BK_OK)
253: 	{
254: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_fault_cnt++;
255: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_fault_cnt |= 0x40000000;
256: 
257: 		return 2;
258: 	}
259: 
260: 	s_mailbox_tx_cnt++;
261: 
262: 	log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_state = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
263: 
264: 	if(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_isr != NULL)
265: 	{
266: 		log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_isr(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].isr_param);  	/* phy_chnl is BUSY now, tx_isr will not trigger phy_chnl_start_tx. */
267: 	}
268: 
269: 	return 0;
270: }
271: 
272: static void mb_phy_chnl_rx_ack_isr(mb_phy_chnl_ack_t *ack_ptr)
273: {
274: 	u8		log_chnl;
275: 	u8		ret_code;
276: 	u8		phy_chnl_idx;
277: 	u8		log_chnl_idx;
278: 
279: 	mb_phy_chnl_cb_t * phy_chnl_ptr;
280: 	mb_log_chnl_cb_t * log_chnl_cb_x;
281: 
282: 	log_chnl = ack_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl;
283: 
284: 	phy_chnl_idx = GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl);   // = DST_CPU_ID;
285: 	log_chnl_idx = GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(log_chnl);
286: 
287: 	s_mailbox_tx_ack_cnt++;

449: static void mb_phy_chnl_rx_cmd_isr(mb_phy_chnl_cmd_t *cmd_ptr)
450: {
451: 	phy_chnnl_hdr_t  chnl_hdr;
452: 	u8			log_chnl = cmd_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl;
453: 	bk_err_t	ret_code;
454: 	u16 		chnl_type;

457: 	u8		log_chnl_idx;

460: 	mb_log_chnl_cb_t * log_chnl_cb_x;
461: 
462: 	phy_chnl_idx = GET_SRC_CPU_ID(log_chnl);   // = SRC_CPU_ID; from SRC_CPU.
463: 	log_chnl_idx = GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(log_chnl);
464: 
465: 	s_mailbox_rx_cnt++;
466: 
467: 	if(SELF_CPU != GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl))
468: 		return;
469:

471: 		return;
472: 
473: 	if(phy_chnl_idx >= PHY_CHNL_NUM)
474: 		return;
475: 
476: 	phy_chnl_ptr = &phy_chnl_x_cb[phy_chnl_idx];
477: 	log_chnl_cb_x = (mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)(phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[phy_chnl_idx]);
478: 
479: 	chnl_hdr.data = cmd_ptr->hdr.data;
480: 
481: 	if(log_chnl_idx >= phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx])
482: 	{
483: 		phy_chnl_ptr->rx_fault_cnt++;
484: 		phy_chnl_ptr->rx_fault_cnt |= 0x80000000;
485: 
486: 		return;
487: 	}
488: 
489: 	if(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].rx_isr != NULL)
490: 	{
491: 		/* clear all other hdr members except hdr.cmd. */
492: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl = 0;
493: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.tx_seq       = 0;
494: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.ctrl         = 0;
495: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.state        = 0;
496: 
497: 		log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].rx_isr(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].isr_param, (mb_chnl_cmd_t *)cmd_ptr);
498: 
499: 		/* !!!! cmd_ptr buffer now contains ACK data !!!!. */
500: 	}
501: 	else
502: 	{
503: 		chnl_hdr.state |= CHNL_STATE_COM_FAIL;		/* cmd NO target app, it is an ACK bit to peer CPU. */
504: 	}
505: 
506: 	if(chnl_hdr.ctrl & CHNL_CTRL_SYNC_TX)
507: 	{
508: 		/* sync tx cmd, do NOT send ACK. */
509: 		return;
510: 	}
511: 
512: 	/* mb_phy_chnl_tx_ack. */
513: 
514: 	/* RE-USE the cmd buffer for ACK !!! */
515: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.data  = chnl_hdr.data;
516: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.ctrl |= CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX;			/* ACK msg, use the ACK channel.  */
517: 
518: 	chnl_type = MB_PHY_ACK_CHNL;

520: 	mailbox_endpoint_t    dst_cpu = (mailbox_endpoint_t)(phy_chnl_idx);

522: 	ret_code = bk_mailbox_send_safe((mailbox_data_t *)cmd_ptr, SELF_CPU, dst_cpu, (void *)&chnl_type);	/* mb_phy_chnl_tx_ack. */
523: 
524: 	if(ret_code != BK_OK)
525: 	{
526: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_fault_cnt++;
527: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_fault_cnt |= 0x80000000;
528: 
529: 		return;
530: 	}
531: 
532: 	s_mailbox_rx_ack_cnt++;
533: 	return;

563: static void mb_phy_chnl_start_tx(u8 log_chnl)
564: {

566: 
567: 	u8		phy_chnl_idx;

569: 	mb_phy_chnl_cb_t * phy_chnl_ptr;

571: 	phy_chnl_idx = GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl);   // = DST_CPU_ID;

574: 		return;
575: 
576: 	if(phy_chnl_idx >= PHY_CHNL_NUM)
577: 		return;

579: 	phy_chnl_ptr = &phy_chnl_x_cb[phy_chnl_idx];

581: 	if(phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state == CHNL_STATE_IDLE)
582: 	{
583: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state = CHNL_STATE_BUSY;		/* MUST set channel state to BUSY firstly. */
584: 		phy_chnl_ptr->busy_since_ms = rtos_get_time();
585: 		/* start_tx->tx_cmd->tx_isr callback->mb_chnl_write->start_tx, it is a loop.
586: 		   break the loop by setting the phy_chnl_cb.tx_state to busy. */
587: 
588: 		ret_code = mb_phy_chnl_tx_cmd(log_chnl);
589: 
590: 		if(ret_code != 0)
591: 		{
592: 			/* tx_cmd failed before the data hit hardware: roll back BOTH
593: 			 * physical and logical state, so the caller can retry and so
594: 			 * the logical channel does not stay BUSY forever. */
595: 			u8                   log_chnl_idx_fail = GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(log_chnl);
596: 			mb_log_chnl_cb_t    *log_chnl_cb_x_fail =
597: 				(mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)(phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[phy_chnl_idx]);

599: 			if (log_chnl_idx_fail < phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx]) {

601: 			}
602: 			phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
603: 			phy_chnl_ptr->busy_since_ms = 0;
604: 		}
605: 	}
606: 
607: 	return;

226: static bool mb_chnl_rx_ready(void)

229: 	 * A command must not be consumed and its business callback run if its
230: 	 * transport ACK cannot be queued. */

234: static void mb_chnl_ack_retry(void)
235: {
236: 	u16 chnl_type = MB_PHY_ACK_CHNL;
237: 
238: 	while (1)
239: 	{
240: 		mb_ack_entry_t entry;
241: 		bk_err_t ret;
242: 		u32 flags = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
243: 
244: 		if (!ack_count || ack_sending)
245: 		{
246: 			mb_chnl_exit_critical(flags);
247: 			return;
248: 		}
249: 		entry = ack_queue[ack_read];
250: 		ack_sending = 1;
251: 		mb_chnl_exit_critical(flags);
252: 
253: 		ret = bk_mailbox_send_safe(&entry.data, SELF_CPU,
254: 			(mailbox_endpoint_t)entry.destination, &chnl_type);
255: 		flags = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
256: 		if (ret != BK_OK)
257: 		{
258: 			phy_chnl_x_cb[entry.destination].ack_retry_cnt++;
259: 			ack_sending = 0;
260: 			mb_chnl_exit_critical(flags);
261: 			return;
262: 		}
263: 		ack_read = (ack_read + 1) % MB_ACK_QUEUE_LEN;
264: 		ack_count--;
265: 		ack_sending = 0;
266: 		mb_chnl_exit_critical(flags);
267: 		s_mailbox_rx_ack_cnt++;
268: 		mb_chnl_notify((mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[entry.destination],
269: 			phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[entry.destination],
270: 			MB_CHNL_EVENT_RX_ACK_SENT);
271: 	}
272: }

274: static bool mb_chnl_ack_enqueue(u8 destination, const mailbox_data_t *data)
275: {
276: 	u32 flags = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
277: 	mb_ack_entry_t *entry;
278: 
279: 	if (ack_count >= MB_ACK_QUEUE_LEN - 1)
280: 	{
281: 		phy_chnl_x_cb[destination].ack_queue_full_cnt++;
282: 		mb_chnl_exit_critical(flags);
283: 		return false;
284: 	}
285: 	entry = &ack_queue[ack_write];
286: 	entry->data = *data;
287: 	entry->destination = destination;
288: 	ack_write = (ack_write + 1) % MB_ACK_QUEUE_LEN;
289: 	ack_count++;
290: 	mb_chnl_exit_critical(flags);
291: 	mb_chnl_ack_retry();
292: 	return true;
293: }

342: 	u16 			chnl_type;
343: 	u8				phy_chnl_idx = GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl);   // = DST_CPU_ID;
344: 	u8				log_chnl_idx = GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(log_chnl);
345: 
346: 	mb_phy_chnl_cb_t * phy_chnl_ptr;
347: 	mb_log_chnl_cb_t * log_chnl_cb_x;
348: 
349: #if !CONFIG_SOC_SMP
350: 	/* for SMP project, log_chnl is always built by CPU0. it is always failed when call this API in CPU1. */
351: 	if(SELF_CPU != GET_SRC_CPU_ID(log_chnl))
352: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
353: #endif
354: 
355: 	if(SELF_CPU == phy_chnl_idx)  // transferred to self.
356: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
357: 
358: 	if(phy_chnl_idx >= PHY_CHNL_NUM)
359: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
360: 
361: 	phy_chnl_ptr = &phy_chnl_x_cb[phy_chnl_idx];
362: 	log_chnl_cb_x = (mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)(phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[phy_chnl_idx]);
363: 
364: 	if(log_chnl_idx >= phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx])
365: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
366: 
367: 	phy_chnl_ptr->tx_seq++;
368: 	phy_chnl_ptr->tx_log_chnl = log_chnl;
369: 
370: 	cmd_ptr = (mb_phy_chnl_cmd_t *)&log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].chnnl_tx_buff;
371: 
372: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl = log_chnl;
373: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.tx_seq = phy_chnl_ptr->tx_seq;
374: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.ctrl  = 0;
375: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.state = 0;
376: 
377: 	phy_chnl_ptr->tx_hdr_cmd = cmd_ptr->hdr.cmd;
378: 	phy_chnl_ptr->last_cmd_header = cmd_ptr->hdr.data;
379: 
380: 	phy_chnl_ptr->param1 = cmd_ptr->param1;
381: 	phy_chnl_ptr->param2 = cmd_ptr->param2;
382: 	phy_chnl_ptr->param3 = cmd_ptr->param3;
383: 
384: 	__DMB();
385: 	chnl_type = MB_PHY_CMD_CHNL;
386: 
387: 	mailbox_endpoint_t    dst_cpu = (mailbox_endpoint_t)(phy_chnl_idx);
388: 
389: 	ret_code = bk_mailbox_send(&log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].chnnl_tx_buff, SELF_CPU, dst_cpu, (void *)&chnl_type);
390: 
391: 	if(ret_code != BK_OK)
392: 	{
393: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_fault_cnt++;
394: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_fault_cnt |= 0x40000000;
395: 
396: 		return ret_code;
397: 	}
398: 
399: 	s_mailbox_tx_cnt++;
400: 
401: 	log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_state = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
402: 
403: 	if(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_isr != NULL)
404: 	{
405: 		log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_isr(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].isr_param);  	/* phy_chnl is BUSY now, tx_isr will not trigger phy_chnl_start_tx. */
406: 	}
407: 
408: 	return BK_OK;
409: }

411: void mb_chnl_start_service(void)

413: 	/* Mailbox RX and ACK dispatch run in the hardware ISR path.  Retain this
414: 	 * legacy entry point for callers, but do not start a second poll model. */

417: static void mb_phy_chnl_rx_ack_isr(mb_phy_chnl_ack_t *ack_ptr)
418: {
419: 	u8		log_chnl;
420: 	u8		ret_code;
421: 	u8		phy_chnl_idx;
422: 	u8		log_chnl_idx;
423: 
424: 	mb_phy_chnl_cb_t * phy_chnl_ptr;
425: 	mb_log_chnl_cb_t * log_chnl_cb_x;
426: 
427: 	log_chnl = ack_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl;
428: 	if (ack_ptr->hdr.ctrl & CHNL_CTRL_RESET)
429: 	{
430: 		mb_chnl_ack_t failure;
431: 
432: 		phy_chnl_idx = GET_SRC_CPU_ID(log_chnl);
433: 		if (ack_ptr->hdr.ctrl != (CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX | CHNL_CTRL_RESET) ||
434: 			ack_ptr->hdr.state != 0 || ack_ptr->hdr.cmd != 0 ||
435: 			ack_ptr->hdr.tx_seq != 0 || ack_ptr->data1 != 0 ||
436: 			ack_ptr->data2 != 0 || ack_ptr->data3 != 0 ||
437: 			GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl) != SELF_CPU ||
438: 			phy_chnl_idx == SELF_CPU || phy_chnl_idx >= PHY_CHNL_NUM)
439: 		{
440: 			s_mailbox_tx_ack_fault_mask |= 0x10;
441: 			if (phy_chnl_idx < PHY_CHNL_NUM)
442: 				phy_chnl_x_cb[phy_chnl_idx].reset_bad_cnt++;
443: 			return;
444: 		}
445: 
446: 		phy_chnl_ptr = &phy_chnl_x_cb[phy_chnl_idx];
447: 		phy_chnl_ptr->recovering = 1;
448: 		log_chnl_cb_x = (mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[phy_chnl_idx];
449: 		mb_chnl_notify(log_chnl_cb_x,
450: 				   phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx],
451: 				   MB_CHNL_EVENT_PEER_RESET);
452: 		u32 reset_flags = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
453: 		if (phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state == CHNL_STATE_BUSY)
454: 		{
455: 			phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
456: 			phy_chnl_ptr->busy_since_ms = 0;
457: 			mb_chnl_exit_critical(reset_flags);
458: 			log_chnl_idx = GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(phy_chnl_ptr->tx_log_chnl);
459: 			if (log_chnl_idx < phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx] &&
460: 				log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_cmpl_isr)
461: 			{
462: 				memset(&failure, 0, sizeof(failure));
463: 				failure.hdr.cmd = phy_chnl_ptr->tx_hdr_cmd;
464: 				failure.hdr.state = CHNL_STATE_COM_FAIL;
465: 				log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_cmpl_isr(
466: 					log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].isr_param, &failure);
467: 			}
468: 			bk_mailbox_tx_timeout((mailbox_endpoint_t)phy_chnl_idx);
469: 		}
470: 		else
471: 			mb_chnl_exit_critical(reset_flags);
472: 		mb_chnl_fail_pending(log_chnl_cb_x,
473: 				     phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx]);
474: 		return;
475: 	}
476:

586: 	phy_chnnl_hdr_t  chnl_hdr;
587: 	u8			log_chnl = cmd_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl;
588: 
589: 	u8		phy_chnl_idx;
590: 	u8		log_chnl_idx;

592: 	mb_phy_chnl_cb_t * phy_chnl_ptr;
593: 	mb_log_chnl_cb_t * log_chnl_cb_x;
594: 
595: 	phy_chnl_idx = GET_SRC_CPU_ID(log_chnl);   // = SRC_CPU_ID; from SRC_CPU.
596: 	log_chnl_idx = GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(log_chnl);
597: 
598: 	s_mailbox_rx_cnt++;
599: 
600: 	if(SELF_CPU != GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl))
601: 		return;
602: 
603: 	if(SELF_CPU == phy_chnl_idx)  // received from self.
604: 		return;
605: 
606: 	if(phy_chnl_idx >= PHY_CHNL_NUM)
607: 		return;
608: 
609: 	phy_chnl_ptr = &phy_chnl_x_cb[phy_chnl_idx];
610: 	log_chnl_cb_x = (mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)(phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[phy_chnl_idx]);
611: 
612: 	chnl_hdr.data = cmd_ptr->hdr.data;
613: 
614: 	if(log_chnl_idx >= phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx])
615: 	{
616: 		phy_chnl_ptr->rx_fault_cnt++;
617: 		phy_chnl_ptr->rx_fault_cnt |= 0x80000000;
618: 
619: 		return;
620: 	}
621: 
622: 	if(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].rx_status_isr != NULL)
623: 	{
624: 		/* clear all other hdr members except hdr.cmd. */
625: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl = 0;
626: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.tx_seq       = 0;
627: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.ctrl         = 0;
628: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.state        = 0;
629: 
630: 		if (log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].rx_status_isr(
631: 			log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].isr_param,
632: 			(mb_chnl_cmd_t *)cmd_ptr) != BK_OK)
633: 			chnl_hdr.state |= CHNL_STATE_COM_FAIL;
634: 	}
635: 	else if(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].rx_isr != NULL)
636: 	{
637: 		/* clear all other hdr members except hdr.cmd. */
638: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl = 0;
639: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.tx_seq       = 0;
640: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.ctrl         = 0;
641: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.state        = 0;

643: 		log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].rx_isr(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].isr_param, (mb_chnl_cmd_t *)cmd_ptr);
644: 
645: 		/* !!!! cmd_ptr buffer now contains ACK data !!!!. */
646: 	}
647: 	else
648: 	{
649: 		memset(cmd_ptr, 0, sizeof(*cmd_ptr));
650: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.data = chnl_hdr.data;

661: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.data  = chnl_hdr.data;
662: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.ctrl |= CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX;			/* ACK msg, use the ACK channel.  */

667: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_fault_cnt |= 0x80000000;
668: 		return;
669: 	}
670: 	return;

673: static void mb_phy_chnl_rx_isr(mailbox_data_t * mb_data)

678: 	rx_data.mb_data.param1 = mb_data->param1;
679: 	rx_data.mb_data.param2 = mb_data->param2;
680: 	rx_data.mb_data.param3 = mb_data->param3;
681: 	/* the following process will damage the input parameter,
682: 	so pass in the pointer of copied parameter instad of the original. */
683: 
684: 	/*
685: 	 *  there are 2 boxes in one MAILBOXn HW,
686: 	 *  but no way to know which box this msg is from in current mailbox_driver design.
687: 	 *  so use the CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX bit in the msg hdr.ctrl to distinguish where it is from.
688: 	 *  when CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX is set, it means from ack box ( MAILBOXn_BOX1 ).

690: 	if(rx_data.phy_ch_hdr.ctrl & CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX)		/* rx ack. */
691: 	{
692: 		mb_phy_chnl_rx_ack_isr(&rx_data.phy_ch_ack);
693: 	}
694: 	else		/* rx cmd. */
695: 	{
696: 		mb_phy_chnl_rx_cmd_isr(&rx_data.phy_ch_cmd);
697: 	}

57: static void mbox0_reap_slots(u8 dst)
58: {
59: 	mbox0_tx_slots_t *slots;
60: 	uint32_t fifo_count;
61: 	u32 reaped = 0;
62: 	u32 now;
63: 	u8 i;
64: 
65: 	if (mbox0_drv_get_send_count(dst, &fifo_count) != MBOX0_HAL_OK)
66: 		return;
67: 
68: 	slots = &mailbox_slots[dst];
69: 	if (fifo_count != 0)
70: 	{
71: 		slots->fifo_empty_since_ms = 0;
72: 		return;
73: 	}
74: 
75: 	now = rtos_get_time();
76: 	if (!slots->fifo_empty_since_ms)
77: 	{
78: 		slots->fifo_empty_since_ms = now ? now : 1;
79: 		return;
80: 	}
81: 	if ((u32)(now - slots->fifo_empty_since_ms) <
82: 		MBOX0_SLOT_QUARANTINE_MS)
83: 		return;
84: 
85: 	for (i = 0; i < MBOX0_CMD_SLOT_NUM; i++)
86: 	{
87: 		reaped += slots->cmd_used[i] != 0;
88: 		slots->cmd_used[i] = 0;
89: 	}
90: 	/* The hardware FIFO contains pointers into these slots.  Once it has
91: 	 * remained empty for the quarantine interval, the peer has had ample time
92: 	 * to copy every published entry.  ACK-only AP traffic has no later command
93: 	 * fence, so retaining these slots indefinitely exhausts the pool during
94: 	 * RESET/STATE/PWC bring-up.
95: 	 */
96: 	for (i = 0; i < MBOX0_ACK_SLOT_NUM; i++)
97: 	{
98: 		reaped += slots->ack_used[i] != 0;
99: 		slots->ack_used[i] = 0;
100: 	}
101: 	reaped += slots->reset_used != 0;
102: 	reaped += slots->sync_used != 0;
103: 	slots->reset_used = 0;
104: 	slots->sync_used = 0;
105: 	slots->cmd_active = 0;
106: 	slots->fifo_empty_since_ms = 0;
107: 	adapter_diag.tx_reaped += reaped;

...

ret = sched_setaffinity(0, sizeof(cpuset), &cpuset);
```

This ordering is intentional and should not be reversed. The project’s own notes document that sending an SMP IPI too early, during the secondary boot/exception-return window, caused a startup regression:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md:694-706`

- `wait_secondary_scheduler()` at `bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:171-188`
- the call at `bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1090`

That is the correct general ordering.

## 4.5 `sched_setaffinity()` can itself invoke scheduler migration

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_setaffinity.c:74-159`

The implementation:

1. finds the TCB;
2. enters a critical section;
3. changes `tcb->affinity`;
4. if the task is running on a CPU no longer allowed, calls `nxsched_set_priority()` to move it;
5. leaves the critical section.

The migration path is therefore not a simple field assignment. It can enter scheduler reprioritization and SMP delivery.

In particular:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_setpriority.c:84-104`

When a running task’s affinity no longer contains its current CPU, NuttX may call:

```c
nxsched_deliver_task(this_cpu(), tcb->cpu, SWITCH_EQUAL);
```

If the board pthread really is already running on CPU0, this path should be inexpensive. If the pthread attribute was not honored, or if the logical/physical CPU mapping is not what the caller assumes, `sched_setaffinity(0, CPU0)` can become the first point where an SMP migration/scheduling IPI is generated.

# 5. BK7258 CPU and mailbox affinity constraints

The AP has two NuttX logical CPUs:

- logical CPU0: the primary AP CPU;
- logical CPU1: the secondary AP CPU, referred to in some project notes as physical CPU2;
- the CP is a separate processor and is not a NuttX SMP CPU.

The physical mailbox send path enforces an AP-only restriction:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mbox0.c:112-128`

```c
int cpu = up_cpu_index();

#ifdef CONFIG_SMP
if (cpu == 1 && (destination != 1 || data[1] != 0))
  {
    return -EPERM;
  }
#endif
```

Therefore an AP logical CPU1 caller cannot send ordinary physical CP descriptors. The transport deliberately routes logical requests through a CPU0-bound worker.

The timer has the same CPU0-only requirement:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_timerisr.c:63-75`

```c
if (up_cpu_index() != 0)
  {
    return -EXDEV;
  }
```

The timer ISR itself runs:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_timerisr.c:38-60`

It calls:

```c
bk7258_smp_retry_pending();
nxsched_process_timer();
```

The current code does not start SysTick until:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1134-1147`

```c
ret = bk7258_timer_start();
...
g_workers_started = true;
return OK;
```

This is the key sequencing problem: after line 1138 succeeds, the global tick is live, but `mb-uart0` has not yet been created.

The project’s historical notes independently identify this class of issue:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md:448-451`

  SysTick was intentionally delayed until after CPU2 handshake and scheduler startup because the first tick could preempt the secondary CPU’s IRQ-restore/exception-return window.

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md:665-675`

  The notes describe the impact of starting the timer before the bring-up thread was safely CPU0-bound.

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md:694-706`

  They document that affinity changes and SMP calls during the sensitive secondary startup window caused a regression, and that the current ordering waits until the secondary scheduler is ready before doing those operations.

The historical log also records a point where the AP had completed mailbox worker creation and then stopped later:

- `README.md:464-473`

This is relevant because it demonstrates that “mailbox workers created” and “system is making scheduler/mailbox progress” are separate milestones.

# 7. Concrete likely root causes

## Root cause 1 — SysTick is enabled before `mb-uart0` is created

**Likelihood: highest.**

Current order:

```text
bk7258_mailbox_workers_start()
  -> create mbox-v2
  -> create mbox-diag
  -> bk7258_timer_start()
  -> return OK

bk7258_mb_uart_worker_start()
  -> kthread_create("mb-uart0", ...)
```

Exact locations:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1112-1125`
- same file, `:1138`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:56-72`

After line 1138, CPU0 can take SysTick interrupts while the parent is creating the UART worker. The timer ISR enters NuttX scheduler/timer code:

- `bk7258_timerisr()`: `bk7258_timerisr.c:38-60`
- scheduler timer processing: `bk7258_timerisr.c:52`

The first tick can also process pending SMP scheduling work:

```c
bk7258_smp_retry_pending();
nxsched_process_timer();
```

This is particularly dangerous on this port because the project history documents real first-tick and SMP scheduler stalls:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md:382-420`
- `:448-451`
- `:665-675`

A `kthread_create()` call performed while the scheduler is being interrupted or while another core is holding the global scheduler spinlock can appear to stop in:

- `kmm_zalloc()` / `nxtask_init()`;
- the scheduler setup critical section;
- `nxtask_activate()`;
- `nxsched_add_readytorun()`;
- an SMP schedule IPI path.

This is the first experiment I recommend.

### Minimal AP-only fix

Create all three deferred workers before enabling SysTick. In practical terms:

- move `bk7258_timer_start()` out of `bk7258_mailbox_workers_start()`;
- create `mb-uart0` first;
- then start SysTick;
- then raise `mbox-v2` and `mb-uart0` to their active priorities.

Preserve the current ordering that waits for the secondary scheduler before changing affinity:

```text
wait_secondary_scheduler()
  -> pin creator CPU0
  -> create workers
  -> start timer
```

Do not move the affinity operation ahead of `wait_secondary_scheduler()`; the project history shows that doing so can send an SMP IPI during the sensitive secondary startup window.

A minimally invasive variant for the experiment is to create `mb-uart0` before the call at `bk7258_bringup.c:56`, then leave the timer start where it is. The cleaner structural fix is to make timer start a separate final step after the UART worker TCB has been created.

## Root cause 2 — “Mailbox workers started successfully” only means their TCBs were activated

**Likelihood: high as a diagnostic/logic problem; it may conceal the real failure.**

`bk7258_mailbox_workers_start()` sets:

```c
g_tx_worker_created = true;
```

at:

- `bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1119-1121`

and:

```c
g_diag_worker_created = true;
```

at:

- `:1131-1132`

It then sets `g_workers_started = true` at:

- `:1145`

None of these points prove that the corresponding worker entry function executed.

The worker may not run before the parent continues because:

- the parent bring-up pthread has priority 100;
- `mbox-v2` and `mb-uart0` initially have priority 95;
- `mbox-diag` has priority 80;
- all are on CPU0.

The normal scheduler behavior is therefore:

```text
parent priority 100 continues
worker priority 95 is runnable but does not preempt parent
kthread_create returns
```

That is normal and not itself a hang.

### Minimal AP-only fix

Add a bounded worker-ready handshake, following the already existing PWC pattern:

- worker posts a semaphore after successful `sched_setaffinity()`;
- creator waits for the post with a finite timeout;
- worker bind failure is propagated;
- do not set `g_worker_created`/`g_workers_started` until the handshake succeeds.

For `mb-uart0`, the worker-ready point should be immediately after:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mb_uart.c:455-459`

For `mbox-v2`, it should be after:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:966-980`

Use the PWC implementation as the model:

- `bk7258_pm_pwc.c:334-347`
- `bk7258_pm_pwc.c:479-493`

Because the current timer is started before `mb-uart0` creation, a timed ready wait currently has a dependency on SysTick. If timer ordering is changed, either:

1. start SysTick after all TCBs are created and then perform the ready waits; or
2. use an atomic/non-blocking readiness flag for the pre-tick creation experiment, followed by a bounded wait after timer start.

## Root cause 3 — Affinity migration may still be incomplete or the CPU identity may be wrong

**Likelihood: medium, but important on this port.**

The board sets the pthread attribute to CPU0:

- `bk7258_bringup.c:216-220`

The NuttX pthread implementation applies that attribute before activation:

- `pthread_create.c:411-423`

That is stronger than a worker calling `sched_setaffinity()` after it starts.

However:

- the return value of `pthread_attr_setaffinity_np()` is ignored;
- the board does not log the actual affinity or `up_cpu_index()`;
- `bk7258_mailbox_workers_start()` calls `sched_setaffinity()` again;
- NuttX affinity changes can enter scheduler migration logic;
- the project history explicitly records cases where a task configured for CPU0 was still observed on the other AP logical CPU while its affinity was being changed.

The worker bind path is:

- mailbox worker: `bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:158-168`
- UART worker: `bk7258_mb_uart.c:97-107`, called at `:455`

The current `bk7258_timer_start()` check gives one useful constraint:

- if `bk7258_mailbox_workers_start()` reaches `g_workers_started = true`, then the caller observed `up_cpu_index() == 0` at `bk7258_timerisr.c:65`.

That reduces the likelihood that the parent was still physically running on CPU1 at the exact timer-start point, but it does not prove that:

- the pthread was CPU0-bound throughout;
- each newly created worker was first scheduled on CPU0;
- the affinity migration path did not trigger a problematic IPI;
- the worker later remained CPU0-bound.

### Minimal AP-only fix

Keep the current “wait secondary first, then pin creator” ordering, but add explicit verification:

- immediately on entry to `bk7258_bringup_worker()`;
- immediately before `bk7258_mailbox_workers_start()`;
- after `sched_setaffinity()` at `bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1103`;
- at the first instruction of `mb_uart_worker()`;
- immediately after its `bind_worker_to_primary()` call.

Record:

```text
up_cpu_index()
this_cpu()
sched_getaffinity(0, ...)
sched_lockcount()
```

Do not treat a worker-side `sched_setaffinity()` call as a readiness barrier. It is a state change plus possible scheduler migration, not proof that the worker has completed migration.

## Root cause 4 — Scheduler or critical-section deadlock triggered by the first tick or SMP delivery

**Likelihood: medium-high if the call truly never returns.**

The exact NuttX activation boundary is:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/task/task_activate.c:64-109`

The SMP delivery boundary is:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_addreadytorun.c:247-270`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/sched/sched.h:489-509`
- BK7258 kick path: `bk7258_smpcall.c:78-123`
- BK7258 scheduler IPI entry: `bk7258_smpcall.c:125-190`
- NuttX delivered-task processing: `sched_process_delivered.c:63-100`

A true no-return symptom after timer activation could result from:

- CPU0 entering the first SysTick and never completing `nxsched_process_timer()`;
- CPU1 holding the global NuttX scheduler lock while stuck in an interrupt or SMP path;
- CPU0 waiting for `g_schedlock`;
- a scheduling IPI being queued but not delivered;
- a remote scheduler callback attempting to operate while the target CPU is still locked;
- the BK7258 raw mailbox kick path failing and leaving the scheduling request pending.

The project’s own history contains evidence of first-tick stalls involving:

- atomics;
- scheduler/timer handling;
- the SMP/exception-return window;
- raw scheduling kicks.

The older observed trace described in the project README:

- `primary=26, secondary=10, detail[2]=0x0f` at `README.md:382-420`

was specifically used to identify a secondary first-tick stop. Although later revisions improved that path, the existence of this failure mode makes the timer-order experiment especially valuable.

### Minimal AP-only fix

If trace confirms the stall at the scheduler/activation boundary:

1. Keep SysTick disabled until all initial worker TCBs exist.
2. Keep the caller on CPU0 before any CPU0-only worker creation.
3. Do not use an extra `sched_lock()` around creation.
4. Audit the BK7258 `up_send_smp_sched()`/raw-kick path for pending-bit and FIFO retry completion.
5. Verify that no board driver holds `g_bk7258_driver_lock` while creating or reprioritizing a task.
6. Temporarily run an AP-only single-logical-CPU experiment (`CONFIG_SMP` disabled or `CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS=1`) only as a diagnostic. If the symptom disappears, it confirms the SMP scheduler/affinity/tick class, not an ordinary heap failure.

## Root cause 5 — Heap/TCB/stack allocation contention or exhaustion

**Likelihood: medium-low for a true hang; high for a fast negative return that is currently not being captured.**

By the time `mb-uart0` is created, the current sequence has allocated:

- the late bring-up pthread stack, 4096 bytes;
- `mbox-v2` TCB and 2048-byte stack;
- `mbox-diag` TCB and 1024-byte stack;
- then it attempts another TCB and 2048-byte stack.

The allocation begins at:

- `task_create.c:93-99`

and the stack allocation occurs through:

- `task_init.c:101-112`.

The expected result is `-ENOMEM`, not a wait. However, the code should print the negative return and allocator state immediately.

The 2048-byte size is not intrinsically invalid. The function signatures match the required NuttX `main_t` form:

```c
static int mb_uart_worker(int argc, char **argv)
```

at:

- `bk7258_mb_uart.c:449`

so a prototype mismatch is not the likely explanation.

### Minimal AP-only fix

Before changing stack size, add a trace around the call and report:

```text
ret
errno
free heap / heap watermark if available
current CPU
scheduler lock count
```

If it returns `-ENOMEM`, test 4096 bytes for `mb-uart0` only or defer another nonessential worker. Do not interpret an allocation failure as an affinity deadlock.

## Root cause 6 — Worker-entry failure is confused with `kthread_create()` failure

**Likelihood: high as an observability problem.**

`mb-uart0` can immediately return:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mb_uart.c:455-459`

if binding fails.

`mbox-v2` can return due to:

- failed affinity at `:966-970`;
- secondary not ready at `:971-975`;
- final error return at `:977-980`.

But `bk7258_mb_uart_worker_start()` sets:

```c
g_worker_created = true;
g_worker_pid = ret;
```

at:

- `bk7258_mb_uart.c:568-570`

without knowing whether the worker has executed.

The same issue applies to `mbox-v2` and `mbox-diag`.

This can produce:

```text
worker-start function appears successful
no worker activity occurs
later transport waits forever or times out
```

It cannot, by itself, make the original `kthread_create()` call fail to return; it can make the surrounding bring-up appear stuck later.

# 8. Why priority 95 is not normally enough to make `kthread_create()` block

The caller’s priority is 100:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:23-24`
- `:214-215`

The new UART worker is created at priority 95:

- `bk7258_mb_uart.c:40`
- `:561-562`

The mailbox TX worker is also created at 95:

- `bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:37`
- `:1112-1113`

The normal SMP activation logic only requests a switch when the new TCB is higher priority than the target CPU’s current task:

- `sched_addreadytorun.c:264-268`

Since 95 is below the bring-up pthread’s 100, normal activation should not preempt the parent. Therefore:

- the worker’s lower priority can delay its first execution;
- it should not prevent `kthread_create()` from returning;
- if `kthread_create()` is genuinely stuck, the first suspects are scheduler/critical-section/tick activity or allocation, not the worker’s loop.

The later `sched_setparam()` raises the worker to 106:

- `bk7258_mb_uart.c:575-586`

That is a separate event and can cause a context switch, but it occurs only after `bk7258_mb_uart_worker_start()` has returned.

```text

# 12. How to interpret the first trace

| Last observed point | Most likely class |
|---|---|
| No marker before `bk7258_mb_uart_worker_start()` | Parent stopped before the call; stage/logging issue |
| Before `nxthread_create()` only | Caller never reached the call or output path is buffered |
| Inside `kmm_zalloc()` | Heap exhaustion/corruption or allocator lock |
| After allocation, before `nxtask_init()` returns | Group, stack, TLS, PID, or task setup |
| At `nxtask_setup_scheduler()` critical section | Scheduler global lock contention |
| `nxtask_activate()` entered but no return | Ready-list insertion, scheduler switch, or SMP scheduling IPI |
| Remote `up_send_smp_sched()` attempted but no send completion | BK7258 raw kick/FIFO/remote-IPI path |
| `kthread_create()` returned a negative value | Ordinary creation failure; inspect errno value, especially `-ENOMEM` |
| `kthread_create()` returned PID but no `mb_uart_worker` entry | Child has not been scheduled yet, or its trace path is broken |
| `mb_uart_worker` entry but bind fails | Affinity/migration/CPU-index issue |
| Worker passes bind but later system stops | Timer, mailbox IRQ, driver-lock, or transport progress problem |
| Timer ISR begins but does not return | First-tick scheduler/atomic/critical-section fault |
| `primary=37` but never `primary=38` | The stall is in UART worker start or the scheduler immediately after mailbox worker startup |

# 13. Recommended minimal fix order

1. **First experiment:** defer `bk7258_timer_start()` until after the `mb-uart0` TCB has been created.
2. **Add before/after trace markers** around the UART `kthread_create()` and inside `nxthread_create()`/`nxtask_activate()`.
3. **Add a bounded ready handshake** to `mb-uart0`; then do the same for `mbox-v2` and `mbox-diag`.
4. **Log actual CPU and affinity**, not just configured affinity.
5. **Verify `sched_lockcount()==0`, interrupt context is false, and no driver spinlock is held** before task creation.
6. **Only if still unresolved, run a one-logical-CPU AP diagnostic build** to isolate SMP.
7. **Only after the scheduler path is cleared, investigate heap size/stack size** and transport-level hangs.

The strongest current conclusion is:

> `bk7258_mailbox_workers_start()` returns after creating two lower-priority TCBs and enabling SysTick. It does not prove that either worker has executed. The immediate subsequent `mb-uart0` creation occurs during the first active AP tick window, while the scheduler and SMP delivery machinery are now live. On this BK7258 port, which has a documented history of first-tick and affinity/remote-IPI timing failures, that is the most credible reason for a perceived no-return at the UART `kthread_create()` boundary. The first AP-only test should move timer activation after the UART TCB creation, while preserving the existing secondary-scheduler wait before CPU0 affinity changes.

置信度中等，判断此论述是否正确：## 1. 哪个函数启动了 tick？

链条（当前最新代码）：


```
up_timer_initialize()            bk7258_timerisr.c:78  ← 只装 handler + 写 RELOAD，不使能
    （nx_start → clock_initialize 时调用）


bk7258_timer_start()              bk7258_timerisr.c:63  ← ★真正启动 tick 的函数
    ├─ putreg32(0, NVIC_SYSTICK_CURRENT)
    ├─ NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL = CLKSOURCE|TICKINT|ENABLE   ← SysTick 从此每1ms触发
    └─ up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_SYSTICK)


调用者：bk7258_mailbox_workers_start()   bk7258_mailbox_channel.c（当前版在两次
        kthread_create 之后调用它，即你的"反序"修复）
再上层：bk7258_bringup() → bringup 线程（bringup.c:56）
```


所以：**handler 注册在 nx_start 早期（up_timer_initialize），但 tick 的使能由 bringup 线程在 late bring-up 中段通过 `bk7258_timer_start()` 完成。**


## 2. 为什么启动 tick 会导致问题？


第一性原理拆解：


**启动 tick 的本质 = 在 CPU0 上开启一个每 1ms 中断一次的 IRQ，而它的 ISR 做的是"真内核工作"：**


```
SysTick ISR (bk7258_timerisr.c:38)
 ├─ bk7258_smp_retry_pending()       → 可能向 CPU2 发 SMP IPI（CH2 FIFO）
 ├─ nxsched_process_timer()
 │    ├─ clock_timer()               → 64位 tick 计数 → 跨核软件原子门（Peterson gate）
 │    ├─ nxsched_process_scheduler() → 双 CPU 的调度器处理 → enter_critical_section(g_schedlock)
 │    └─ watchdog 到期处理
```


而 tick 使能的那一刻，bringup 线程（CPU0, prio100）**恰好正在执行第一批真正的调度操作**——`kthread_create` → `nxsched_add_readytorun` → 任务入队、调度器锁、可能的调度 IPI。于是：


```
时间线（冻结窗口）：
kthread_create("mb-uart0")  ← bringup 线程进入调度器临界区（持锁/持gate/IPI发送中）
        │
        ▼ 1ms 后 tick ISR 抢占（同 CPU）
SysTick ISR 也要碰同一套调度器锁 / 原子门 / IPI
        │
        ▼ 锁不可重入 / 门互斥 / IPI 互等
ISR 以 IRQ 屏蔽状态自旋 → 被抢占的 bringup 线程永远无法恢复 → CPU0 冻结
```


**证据链（已逐次验证）**：
- tick 关闭时：mbox-v2/mbox-diag 的 kthread_create 正常通过（上次启动 P#35 前的两站）；
- tick 一开：紧接着的 mb-uart0 kthread_create 必冻结（primary=37，P#38 永不出现）——**两个不同调用点、同一模式，与 worker 类型无关**；
- secondary=16：CPU2 完整处理过一个调度 IPI——说明调度/IPI 机制在冻结前一刻都正常，冻结是 CPU0 上"tick ISR 与调度器临界区并发"的互等死锁。


**为什么官方 port 没这个问题**：官方 rp2040/esp32 的 tick 在 `nx_start` 就使能、带活 tick 创建线程是常态——因为官方调度器锁（`g_schedlock` rspin）是可重入的、原子操作不走跨核软件 gate。本 port 的独特组合（tick 在 bring-up 中段才开 + 每个原子都过跨核 Peterson gate + SMP IPI 复用共享 mailbox FIFO）把这个"tick 抢占调度临界区"的窗口变成死锁。这正对应 README 排障史里反复出现的同一类故障——"首 tick / 调度 IPI 过早抢占"。


**修复方向的推论**：真正要修的不是"tick 晚开"，而是让 tick ISR 在该窗口内不触碰调度器临界区（tick 只推进时钟+wdog，SMP 调度处理延迟），或修掉锁/门/IPI 的互等路径——需要 tick 活性计数器探针先定位 ISR 卡在哪一段（入口/`smp_retry_pending`/`process_timer`）。

390: /****************************************************************************
391:  * Name: nxthread_setup_scheduler
392:  *
393:  * Description:
394:  *   This functions initializes the common portions of the Task Control Block
395:  *   (TCB) in preparation for starting a new thread.
396:  *
397:  *   nxthread_setup_scheduler() is called from nxtask_setup_scheduler() and
398:  *   pthread_setup_scheduler().
399:  *
400:  * Input Parameters:
401:  *   tcb        - Address of the new task's TCB
402:  *   priority   - Priority of the new task
403:  *   start      - Thread startup routine
404:  *   entry      - Thread user entry point
405:  *   ttype      - Type of the new thread: task, pthread, or kernel thread
406:  *
407:  * Returned Value:
408:  *   OK on success; ERROR on failure.
409:  *
410:  *   This function can only failure is it is unable to assign a new, unique
411:  *   task ID to the TCB (errno is not set).
412:  *
413:  ****************************************************************************/
414: 
415: static int nxthread_setup_scheduler(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb, int priority,
416:                                     start_t start, CODE void *entry,
417:                                     int ttype)
418: {
419:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
420:   irqstate_t flags;
421:   int ret;
422: 
423:   /* Assign a unique task ID to the task. */
424: 
425:   ret = nxtask_assign_pid(tcb);
426:   if (ret == OK)
427:     {
428:       struct tls_info_s *info = tcb->stack_alloc_ptr;
429: 
430:       /* Save PID to TLS */
431: 
432:       info->tl_tid = tcb->pid;
433: 
434:       /* Save task priority and entry point in the TCB */
435: 
436:       tcb->sched_priority = priority;
437:       tcb->init_priority  = priority;
438: #ifdef CONFIG_PRIORITY_INHERITANCE
439:       tcb->base_priority  = (uint8_t)priority;
440: #endif
441:       tcb->start          = start;
442:       tcb->entry.main     = (main_t)entry;
443: 
444:       /* Save the thread type.  This setting will be needed in
445:        * up_initial_state() is called.
446:        */
447: 
448:       ttype              &= TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_MASK;
449:       atomic_and(&tcb->flags, ~TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_MASK);
450:       atomic_or(&tcb->flags, ttype);
451: 
452:       /* Set the appropriate scheduling policy in the TCB */
453: 
454:       atomic_and(&tcb->flags, ~TCB_FLAG_POLICY_MASK);
455: #if CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL > 0
456:       atomic_or(&tcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_SCHED_RR);
457:       tcb->timeslice      = MSEC2TICK(CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL);
458: #else
459:       atomic_or(&tcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_SCHED_FIFO);
460: #endif
461: 
462:       /* Save the task ID of the parent task in the TCB and allocate
463:        * a child status structure.
464:        */
465: 
466:       nxtask_save_parent(tcb, ttype);
467: 
468: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
469:       /* exec(), task_create(), and vfork() all inherit the affinity mask
470:        * from the parent thread.  This is the default for pthread_create()
471:        * as well but the affinity mask can be specified in the pthread
472:        * attributes as well.  pthread_create() will have to fix up the
473:        * affinity mask in this case.
474:        */
475: 
476:       nxtask_inherit_affinity(tcb);
477: #endif
478: 
479:       /* exec(), pthread_create(), task_create(), and vfork() all
480:        * inherit the signal mask of the parent thread.
481:        */
482: 
483:       tcb->sigprocmask = rtcb->sigprocmask;
484: 
485:       /* Initialize the task state.  It does not get a valid state
486:        * until it is activated.
487:        */
488: 
489:       tcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_INVALID;
490: 
491:       /* Clone the parent tasks D-Space (if it was running PIC).  This
492:        * must be done before calling up_initial_state() so that the
493:        * state setup will take the PIC address base into account.
494:        */
495: 
496:       nxtask_dup_dspace(tcb);
497: 
498:       /* Initialize the processor-specific portion of the TCB */
499: 
500:       up_initial_state(tcb);
501: 
502:       /* Add the task to the inactive task list */
503: 
504:       flags = enter_critical_section();
505:       dq_addfirst((FAR dq_entry_t *)tcb, list_inactivetasks());
506:       tcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_INACTIVE;
507:       leave_critical_section(flags);
508:     }
509: 
510:   return ret;
511: }

177:  * Description:
178:  *   If this CPU does not already hold the spinlock, then loop until the
179:  *   spinlock is successfully locked.
180:  *
181:  *   This implementation is non-reentrant and is prone to deadlocks in
182:  *   the case that any logic on the same CPU attempts to take the lock
183:  *   more than once.

185:  * Input Parameters:
186:  *   lock - A reference to the spinlock object to lock.

192:  * Assumptions:

194:  *
195:  ****************************************************************************/
196: 
197: #ifdef CONFIG_SPINLOCK
198: static inline_function void spin_lock(FAR volatile spinlock_t *lock)
199: {
200:   /* Mark that we want to hold lock */
201: 
202:   spinlock_mark_locking(&lock->info);
203: 
204:   /* Notify that we are waiting for a spinlock */
205: 
206:   sched_note_spinlock(lock, NOTE_SPINLOCK_LOCK);

208:   /* If CONFIG_SCHED_CRITMONITOR_MAXTIME_BUSYWAIT >= 0, count busy-waiting. */

220:   /* Get the lock, end counting busy-waiting */

222:   nxsched_critmon_busywait(false, return_address(0));

400: /****************************************************************************
401:  * Name: wd_timer
402:  *
403:  * Description:
404:  *   This function is called from the timer interrupt handler to determine
405:  *   if it is time to execute a watchdog function.  If so, the watchdog
406:  *   function will be executed in the context of the timer interrupt
407:  *   handler.
408:  *
409:  * Input Parameters:
410:  *   ticks - If CONFIG_SCHED_TICKLESS is defined then the number of ticks
411:  *     in the interval that just expired is provided.  Otherwise,
412:  *     this function is called on each timer interrupt and a value of one
413:  *     is implicit.
414:  *   noswitches - True: Can't do context switches now.
415:  *
416:  * Returned Value:
417:  *   If CONFIG_SCHED_TICKLESS is defined then the number of ticks for the
418:  *   next delay is provided (CLOCK_MAX if no delay). Otherwise, this function
419:  *   has no returned value.
420:  *
421:  * Assumptions:
422:  *   Called from interrupt handler logic with interrupts disabled.
423:  *
424:  ****************************************************************************/
425: 
426: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_TICKLESS
427: clock_t wd_timer(clock_t ticks, bool noswitches)
428: {
429:   FAR struct wdog_s *wdog;
430:   irqstate_t flags;
431:   clock_t    ret = CLOCK_MAX;
432: 
433:   /* Check if the watchdog at the head of the list is ready to run */
434: 
435:   if (!noswitches)
436:     {
437:       ret = wd_expiration(ticks);
438:     }
439:   else
440:     {
441:       flags = enter_critical_section();
442: 
443:       /* Return the delay for the next watchdog to expire */
444: 
445:       if (!list_is_empty(&g_wdactivelist))
446:         {
447:           /* Notice that if noswitches, expired - g_wdtickbase
448:            * may get negative value.
449:            */
450: 
451:           wdog = list_first_entry(&g_wdactivelist, struct wdog_s, node);
452:           ret  = !clock_compare(wdog->expired, ticks) ?
453:                  wdog->expired - ticks : 0u;
454:         }
455: 
456:       leave_critical_section(flags);
457:     }
458: 
459:   return ret;
460: }
461: 
462: #else
463: void wd_timer(clock_t ticks)
464: {
465:   /* Check if there are any active watchdogs to process */
466: 
467:   wd_expiration(ticks);
468: }
469: #endif /* CONFIG_SCHED_TICKLESS */

129: clock_t nxsched_process_roundrobin(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb, clock_t ticks,
130:                                    bool noswitches)
131: {
132:   FAR struct tcb_s *ptcb;  /* Pointer to the next ready-to-run TCB */
133:   clock_t ret;
134:   int decr;
135: 
136:   /* How much can we decrement the timeslice delay?  If 'ticks' is greater
137:    * than the timeslice value, then we ignore any excess amount.
138:    *
139:    * 'ticks' should not be greater than the remaining timeslice.  But that
140:    * event seems to be possible, perhaps in cases where pre-emption has been
141:    * disabled or the noswitches flag is set.  This might cause jitter of a
142:    * few ticks in the slicing because the excess amount is not handled.
143:    */
144: 
145:   DEBUGASSERT(tcb != NULL);
146:   decr = MIN(tcb->timeslice, ticks);
147: 
148:   /* Decrement the timeslice counter */
149: 
150:   tcb->timeslice -= decr;
151: 
152:   /* Did decrementing the timeslice counter cause the timeslice to expire? */
153: 
154:   ret = tcb->timeslice;
155:   if (tcb->timeslice <= 0 && !nxsched_islocked_tcb(tcb))
156:     {
157:       /* We will also suppress context switches if we were called via one
158:        * of the unusual cases handled by nxsched_reassess_timer().  In that
159:        * case, we will return a value of one so that the timer will expire
160:        * as soon as possible and we can perform this action in the normal
161:        * timer expiration context.
162:        *
163:        * This is kind of kludge, but I am not to concerned because I hope
164:        * that the situation is impossible or at least could only occur on
165:        * rare corner-cases.
166:        */
167: 
168:       if (noswitches)
169:         {
170:           ret = 0;
171:         }
172:       else
173:         {
174:           /* Reset the timeslice. */
175: 
176:           tcb->timeslice = MSEC2TICK(CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL);
177:           ret = tcb->timeslice;
178: 
179:           /* We know we are at the head of the ready to run prioritized

183:            * give that task a shot.

**结论**

这段论述中：

- **第 1 部分基本正确，置信度高。**
- **第 2 部分把“tick 开启后出现冻结”直接推导为“SysTick 抢占持锁的 `kthread_create()` 并同核死锁”，证据不足，而且关键机制与当前 NuttX 实现不符。**
- 综合判断：**现象关联成立，具体死锁模型目前不成立。整体正确度约 45%，中等置信度。**

**确定正确的部分**

1. `up_timer_initialize()` 只配置 SysTick，不启动计数。

[bk7258_timerisr.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_timerisr.c:78) 中：

```c
putreg32(0, NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL);
putreg32(BK7258_SYSTICK_RELOAD, NVIC_SYSTICK_RELOAD);
irq_attach(...);
```

没有写入 `ENABLE | TICKINT`。

2. `bk7258_timer_start()` 才真正启动 tick。

同文件 [第 63 行](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_timerisr.c:63) 写入：

```c
NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL_CLKSOURCE |
NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL_TICKINT |
NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL_ENABLE
```

3. 当前调用链描述正确：

```text
bk7258_bringup()
  -> bk7258_mailbox_workers_start()
       -> 创建 mbox-v2
       -> 创建 mbox-diag
       -> bk7258_timer_start()
  -> bk7258_mb_uart_worker_start()
       -> kthread_create("mb-uart0")
```

对应 [bk7258_mailbox_channel.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1110) 和 [bk7258_bringup.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:56)。

4. SysTick ISR 确实执行完整内核 timer 处理：

```c
bk7258_smp_retry_pending();
nxsched_process_timer();
```

`nxsched_process_timer()` 又执行：

```text
clock_timer()
nxsched_process_scheduler()
wd_timer()
```

这一点和源码一致。

**不成立或尚未证明的部分**

1. “SysTick 抢占正在持有调度器锁的 `kthread_create()`”在正常 NuttX 机制下不会发生。

`kthread_create()` 最终进入：

```c
flags = enter_critical_section();
...
nxsched_add_readytorun(tcb);
...
leave_critical_section(flags);
```

参见 [task_activate.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/task/task_activate.c:64)。

SMP 下 `enter_critical_section()` 等价于：

```c
rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_schedlock)
```

参见 [spinlock.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/include/nuttx/spinlock.h:1531)。

它会先执行 `up_irq_save()`。Cortex-M33 上该操作把 `BASEPRI` 设置为 `NVIC_SYSH_DISABLE_PRIORITY`，当前值是默认优先级阈值。SysTick 本身也被设置为默认优先级。因此正常情况下：

```text
CPU0 进入调度器临界区
    -> BASEPRI 屏蔽 SysTick
    -> SysTick 只能 pending
    -> leave_critical_section 后才进入 ISR
```

不是：

```text
持有 g_schedlock
    -> 被 SysTick 抢占
    -> ISR 再次获取同一锁
```

如果实板真的发生后一种情况，首先意味着 `BASEPRI`、SysTick 优先级、安全态中断路由或 IRQ restore 有 port 级错误，不能直接归因于 NuttX 锁不可重入。

2. `g_schedlock` 不是普通不可重入 spinlock。

当前 NuttX 使用 `rspinlock_t`：

```c
DEFINE_PER_CPU_BMP(rspinlock_t, g_schedlock) =
  RSPINLOCK_INITIALIZER;
```

参见 [irq_csection.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/irq/irq_csection.c:44)。

`rspin_lock()` 按 CPU owner 支持递归。因此“官方调度锁可重入，本 port 不可重入”的表述不准确。当前 port 使用的仍是 NuttX `rspinlock_t`。

3. 当前日志反证了“首 tick 卡在 `nxsched_process_timer()`”。

最新日志为：

```text
detail[3] = 00000002
detail[4] = a8000000
```

而 ISR 仅在 `nxsched_process_timer()` 返回后才写入：

```c
bk7258_boottrace_detail(3, 2);
```

因此该日志明确证明：

```text
首个 SysTick 已进入
bk7258_smp_retry_pending() 已返回
nxsched_process_timer() 已完整返回
atomic gate 已释放
```

README 自身也记录了这个结论：

> `detail[3]=2` 证明 `nxsched_process_timer()` 已完整返回；`detail[4]=a8000000` 表示 atomic gate 已完整释放。

所以历史上的“首 tick 卡住”是真实故障，但已经不是当前 `primary=37` 版本的已知停点。

4. `secondary=16` 不能证明 CPU2 处理的一定是调度 IPI。

stage 16 只说明 CPU2 收到并处理了：

```text
BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK
```

RAW kick 内可能包含：

```c
BK7258_IPI_SCHED
BK7258_IPI_CALL
```

stage 本身没有记录 pending bit，也没有证明该 kick 紧邻 `mb-uart0` 创建，更不能据此证明 CPU0 与 CPU2 正在互等。

5. `primary=37` 只提供区间定位。

它证明：

```text
bk7258_mailbox_workers_start() 已返回
bk7258_mb_uart_worker_start() 后的 stage 38 未执行
```

但不能证明：

```text
一定卡在 kthread_create()
```

还可能卡在：

- stage 37 写入后、函数调用前的 IRQ；
- `kthread_create()` 的 TCB 分配；
- stack 分配；
- PID 分配；
- task 初始化；
- `nxtask_activate()`；
- 一次后续 timer/mailbox IRQ；
- HardFault/UsageFault，但异常日志路径不可用。

必须在 `kthread_create()` 内部增加分段探针才能定论。

6. “官方 port 的 atomic 不走跨核 gate”不普遍正确。

例如 RP2040 同样定义了 `g_atomic_hwspinlock`。NuttX 支持使用硬件 spinlock 实现 libc atomic。真正需要证明的是 BK7258 当前 Peterson gate 是否满足：

- 中断上下文递归；
- 双核同时争用；
- owner/depth 发布顺序；
- CPU migration 约束；
- memory attribute 与 barrier；
- panic/exception 路径下的释放。

不能通过和 RP2040/ESP32 的概括比较直接得出结论。

**更准确的当前假设**

可以保留以下弱化表述：

> 启用 SysTick 后，系统新增了每 1 ms 执行一次的 timer、atomic、scheduler 和 watchdog 路径。`primary=37` 之后的冻结可能与 tick 引入的并发有关，但当前日志已经证明首 tick 完整返回；尚不能证明是 SysTick 同核抢占 `kthread_create()` 持锁区导致死锁。更可能的范围是后续 tick、跨核锁竞争、任务创建内部、异常路径或 SMP IPI 状态问题。

**修复方向判断**

“直接让 tick ISR 不执行 scheduler”不适合作为正式修复：

- `nxsched_process_timer()` 是标准 NuttX tick 入口。
- 去掉 scheduler 处理会破坏 RR timeslice。
- 延迟 watchdog 会破坏 semaphore timeout、sleep、worker deadline 和 mailbox recovery。
- `clock_timer()` 本身仍使用 seqlock/atomic，不能完全排除锁问题。
- `bk7258_smp_retry_pending()` 可以临时移除做 A/B 诊断，但不应直接作为最终方案。

更可靠的下一轮探针是：

```text
A: bk7258_mb_uart_worker_start() 入口
B: kthread_create() 前
C: nxthread_create() 入口
D: kmm_zalloc() 返回
E: nxtask_init() 返回
F: nxtask_activate() 前
G: nxsched_add_readytorun() 前后
H: kthread_create() 返回
I: mb_uart_worker() 第一条指令
```

同时把 timer 探针改成持续计数，而不是只记录首 tick：

```text
tick_entry_count
after_smp_retry_count
after_clock_count
after_scheduler_count
after_wdog_count
tick_exit_count
```

并在每个点记录：

```text
IPSR
BASEPRI
PRIMASK
this_cpu()
g_schedlock owner/count

g_ipi_pending[1]
g_ipi_kicked[1]
```

8: # either one produces zero bytes.  That is why a human has to press RST while
9: # bk_loader is looping on "Getting Bus...".
10: #
11: # The bootrom only answers the LinkCheck handshake for a short window after a
12: # reset.  Measured on this board: issuing "reboot" over the CP shell gives
13: # about 473 ms of silence (0.005 s -> 0.478 s) before firmware output starts,
14: # and the shell prompt is back at 1.04 s.  So the window is wide enough.
15: #
16: # bk_loader does not take TIOCEXCL on the tty, so a second process can write
17: # into the same port while bk_loader is looping.  Writing "reboot" there makes
18: # the running firmware reset itself -- exactly what pressing RST does, only
19: # scripted.  Verified: "Gotten Bus..." arrives ~0.5 s after the write.
20: #
21: # IMPORTANT: once the bus is taken, anything else written to the port would
22: # corrupt the protocol, so the reboot loop stops the moment "Gotten Bus"
23: # appears in the log.
24: 
25: set -u
26: 
27: ROOT=/home/mi/vela_competition
28: LOADER="$ROOT/bk_loader"
29: DEFAULT_IMAGE="$ROOT/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/package/all-app.bin"
30: EXPECTED_SIZE=2646016
31: 
32: PORT=/dev/ttyUSB0
33: PORTNUM=0
34: 
35: # Two independent baud rates, do not conflate them.
36: #
37: # BAUD is only how fast bk_loader talks to the bootrom.  CONSOLE_BAUD is what
38: # the firmware's console runs at, which is fixed by the build (defconfig), so
39: # raising the flash speed must not change it.  Using one variable for both
40: # meant that after "-b 1500000" the post-flash screen opened at 1500000 and
41: # nothing typed into it worked.
42: BAUD=115200
43: CONSOLE_BAUD=115200
44: IMAGE="$DEFAULT_IMAGE"
45: LOG=/tmp/autoflash.log
46: REBOOT_TRIES=8
47: REBOOT_INTERVAL=1.5
48: 
49: # Overall timeout is derived from the image size, never hard-coded.
50: #
51: # A fixed 180 s was wrong and actively harmful: 2,646,016 bytes at 115200 baud
52: # is 10 bits per byte on the wire, i.e. ~230 s of writing alone, plus ~10 s of
53: # 64K erase.  timeout(1) killed a real flash at "Writing Flash ... 69%",
54: # leaving the board with an erased-but-incomplete image.  Computed below as
55: # transfer time x 2 plus 60 s of headroom.
56: OVERALL_TIMEOUT=0
57: ATTACH_SERIAL=0
58: SKIP_SIZE_CHECK=0
59: TEST_ONLY=0
60: 
61: usage() {
62:   cat <<'EOF'
63: 用法: autoflash.sh [选项]
64: 
65:   -i <file>    要烧录的镜像，默认 all-app.bin
66:   -p <port>    串口设备，默认 /dev/ttyUSB0
67:   -n <num>     bk_loader 的端口号，默认 0
68:   -b <baud>    烧录波特率，默认 115200（只影响下载速度）
69:   -B <baud>    控制台波特率，默认 115200（固件编译时定死的，一般别改）
70:   -s           跳过 all-app.bin 字节数校验
71:   -a           烧完自动挂上串口看日志
72:   -t           只测握手，不写 flash（用 read 代替 download）
73:   -h           显示本帮助
74: 
75: 说明: 不需要手按 RST。脚本会在 bk_loader 握手循环期间，从另一个进程往
76:       同一个串口写 reboot 来触发软复位。
77: EOF
78: }
79: 
80: while getopts "i:p:n:b:B:sath" opt; do
81:   case "$opt" in
82:     i) IMAGE="$OPTARG" ;;
83:     p) PORT="$OPTARG" ;;
84:     n) PORTNUM="$OPTARG" ;;
85:     b) BAUD="$OPTARG" ;;
86:     B) CONSOLE_BAUD="$OPTARG" ;;
87:     s) SKIP_SIZE_CHECK=1 ;;
88:     a) ATTACH_SERIAL=1 ;;
89:     t) TEST_ONLY=1 ;;
90:     h) usage; exit 0 ;;
91:     *) usage; exit 2 ;;
92:   esac
93: done
94: 
95: die() { echo "错误: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
96: 
97: # ---------------------------------------------------------------- 1. 前置检查
98: 
99: [ -x "$LOADER" ] || die "找不到 bk_loader: $LOADER"
100: [ -f "$IMAGE" ]  || die "找不到镜像: $IMAGE"
101: [ -c "$PORT" ]   || die "串口不存在: $PORT（板子插了吗？）"
102: 
103: SIZE=$(stat -c%s "$IMAGE")
104: SHA=$(sha256sum "$IMAGE" | cut -d' ' -f1)
105: 
106: # 10 bits on the wire per byte (8N1 plus start and stop).
107: XFER_SECS=$(( SIZE * 10 / BAUD ))
108: OVERALL_TIMEOUT=$(( XFER_SECS * 2 + 60 ))
109: 
110: echo "=== 待烧录镜像 ==="
111: echo "  路径   : $IMAGE"
112: echo "  字节数 : $SIZE"
113: echo "  SHA256 : $SHA"
114: echo "  串口   : $PORT"
115: echo "  烧录   : ${BAUD} baud，传输约 ${XFER_SECS}s，超时上限 ${OVERALL_TIMEOUT}s"
116: echo "  控制台 : ${CONSOLE_BAUD} baud（烧完会恢复成这个）"
117: 
118: if [ "$SKIP_SIZE_CHECK" -eq 0 ] && [ "$(basename "$IMAGE")" = "all-app.bin" ]; then
119:   if [ "$SIZE" -ne "$EXPECTED_SIZE" ]; then
120:     die "all-app.bin 应为 $EXPECTED_SIZE 字节，实际 $SIZE。打包可能不完整，用 -s 可跳过此检查"
121:   fi
122:   echo "  字节数校验通过"
123: fi
124: 
125: # ---------------------------------------------------------- 2. 释放串口占用
126: 
127: echo
128: echo "=== 释放串口 ==="
129: HOLDERS=$(fuser "$PORT" 2>/dev/null | tr -s ' ')
130: if [ -n "$HOLDERS" ]; then
131:   echo "  当前占用: $HOLDERS"
132: 
133:   # Detached screen sessions are the usual culprit: Ctrl-A D leaves them
134:   # running and holding the tty.
135:   while read -r sid; do
136:     [ -n "$sid" ] || continue
137:     echo "  关闭 screen 会话 $sid"
138:     screen -X -S "$sid" quit >/dev/null 2>&1
139:   done < <(screen -ls 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '^\s+[0-9]+\.[^ \t]+' | tr -d ' \t')
140: 
141:   pkill -f "cat $PORT" >/dev/null 2>&1
142: 
143:   sleep 0.5
144:   HOLDERS=$(fuser "$PORT" 2>/dev/null | tr -s ' ')
145:   if [ -n "$HOLDERS" ]; then
146:     die "串口仍被占用: $HOLDERS。手动处理后重试（参考 docs/端口冲突解决办法.md）"
147:   fi
148: fi
149: echo "  串口空闲"
150: 
151: # Console baud, not flash baud: the only thing written through this port
152: # before bk_loader takes over is the "reboot" command, and the firmware's
153: # console is listening at CONSOLE_BAUD.
154: stty -F "$PORT" "$CONSOLE_BAUD" cs8 -cstopb -parenb raw -echo -crtscts \
155:   || die "stty 配置失败"
156: 
157: # --------------------------------------------------- 3. 启动 bk_loader 并软复位
158: 
159: echo
160: : > "$LOG"
161: PIDFILE=$(mktemp)
162: 
163: # The in-loop reset works at any -b, and here is why it is safe to rely on:
164: # bk_loader opens the tty at 115200 no matter what -b says, handshakes there,
165: # and only switches to the requested rate once it owns the bus.  Measured from
166: # a real 1500000 run:
167: #
168: #   cmdline: ... bk_loader download -p 0 -b 1500000 ...
169: #   Current port : /dev/ttyUSB0 + BaudRate : 115200 connect success
170: #   Getting Bus... / Gotten Bus... / All Finished Successfully
171: #
172: # So while we are writing "reboot" the line is still at 115200 and the
173: # firmware console decodes it fine.  An earlier version of this script
174: # disabled the retry loop for BAUD != CONSOLE_BAUD on the theory that the port
175: # had already been switched up -- that was reasoning without measurement, and
176: # it broke a mechanism that worked.
177: 
178: if [ "$TEST_ONLY" -eq 1 ]; then
179:   echo "=== 只测握手，不写 flash ==="
180:   set -- read -p "$PORTNUM" -b "$BAUD" -f "/tmp/autoflash_probe.bin@0-1000"
181: else
182:   echo "=== 开始烧录（无需按 RST）==="
183:   set -- download -p "$PORTNUM" -b "$BAUD" -s 0 -i "$IMAGE"
184: fi
185: 
186: # Output goes to the terminal *and* the log.
187: #
188: # bk_loader draws its erase/write progress with cli_printf_progress_bar,
189: # which emits "Erasing Flash ... 42%\r" -- carriage return, no newline.  Two
190: # things are needed to see that live: tee, so the bytes reach the terminal at
191: # all, and stdbuf -o0, because with a pipe on stdout glibc would otherwise
192: # block-buffer 4 KB at a time and the bar would arrive in lurches.
193: #
194: # The PID is stashed in a file because with a pipeline $! would be tee's.
195: (
196:   stdbuf -o0 -e0 timeout "$OVERALL_TIMEOUT" "$LOADER" "$@" &
197:   echo $! > "$PIDFILE"
198:   wait $!
199: ) 2>&1 | tee "$LOG" &
200: PIPELINE_PID=$!
201: 
202: LOADER_PID=""
203: for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
204:   if [ -s "$PIDFILE" ]; then LOADER_PID=$(cat "$PIDFILE"); break; fi
205:   sleep 0.1
206: done
207: [ -n "$LOADER_PID" ] || die "无法获取 bk_loader 进程号"
208: 
209: # Wait for it to actually enter the retry loop before poking the board.
210: for _ in $(seq 1 40); do
211:   grep -q "Getting Bus" "$LOG" && break
212:   kill -0 "$LOADER_PID" 2>/dev/null || break
213:   sleep 0.1
214: done
215: 
216: if ! kill -0 "$LOADER_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
217:   echo "  bk_loader 提前退出:"
218:   tail -5 "$LOG" | sed 's/^/    | /'
219:   wait "$LOADER_PID"; exit 1
220: fi
221: 
222: GOT_BUS=0
223: 
224: echo "  bk_loader 已进入握手循环，开始发送软复位"
225: 
226: for i in $(seq 1 "$REBOOT_TRIES"); do
227:   if grep -aq "Gotten Bus" "$LOG"; then GOT_BUS=1; break; fi
228:   kill -0 "$LOADER_PID" 2>/dev/null || break
229: 
230:   # If the console happens to be bridged to the AP shell, escape back to the
231:   # CP shell first: Ctrl-] then '.'.
232:   #
233:   # The trailing newline after the escape is essential.  Without it the CP
234:   # shell buffers all of it as a single line and sees "\x1d.reboot", answers
235:   # "cmd NOT found: .reboot" and never resets -- which made every attempt here
236:   # fall through to the manual RST prompt.  Measured: with the flush the board
237:   # reboots, without it it never does.
238:   printf '\035' > "$PORT" 2>/dev/null
239:   printf '.'    > "$PORT" 2>/dev/null
240:   printf '\r\n' > "$PORT" 2>/dev/null
241:   printf 'reboot\r\n' > "$PORT" 2>/dev/null
242:   echo "  第 $i 次软复位已发出"
243: 
244:   # Poll frequently so we stop writing the instant the bus is taken --
245:   # further bytes would corrupt the download protocol.
246:   for _ in $(seq 1 15); do
247:     if grep -q "Gotten Bus" "$LOG"; then GOT_BUS=1; break; fi
248:     sleep 0.1
249:   done
250:   [ "$GOT_BUS" -eq 1 ] && break
251: done
252: 
253: if [ "$GOT_BUS" -eq 1 ]; then
254:   echo "  握手成功，下面是 bk_loader 的实时输出："
255: else
256:   echo "  软复位没能拿到总线 —— 现在请手动按一次 RST（按一下就彻底松手）"
257:   echo "  bk_loader 仍在循环握手，按下去就会接上"
258: fi
259: 
260: # Waiting on the pipeline, not the loader: tee has to finish draining before
261: # the log is complete enough to judge the outcome.
262: wait "$PIPELINE_PID"
263: RC=$?
264: rm -f "$PIDFILE"
265: 
266: # ------------------------------------------------------------------ 4. 判定
267: 
268: echo
269: echo "=== 结果 ==="
270: if grep -aq "All Finished Successfully" "$LOG"; then
271:   echo "  烧录成功"
272:   grep -aE "Total Test Time|EraseFlash ->pass" "$LOG" \
273:     | tail -3 | sed 's/^/    | /'
274: else
275:   echo "  烧录失败（退出码 $RC）"
276: 
277:   # Distinguish "never got started" from "killed halfway through the write",
278:   # because the second case leaves the board unbootable and must be re-flashed
279:   # before anything else is attempted.
280:   LAST_PCT=$(tr '\r' '\n' < "$LOG" | grep -aoE "Writing Flash \.\.\. [0-9]+%" \
281:              | tail -1)
282:   if [ -n "$LAST_PCT" ]; then
283:     echo
284:     echo "  !! flash 已被擦除但只写到 $LAST_PCT —— 固件不完整，板子起不来。"
285:     echo "     必须重新完整烧录一次才能恢复。"
286:     echo "     此时固件不响应 reboot，软复位无效，需要手动按一次 RST。"
287:   elif [ "$RC" -eq 124 ]; then
288:     echo "  !! 被超时中止（上限 ${OVERALL_TIMEOUT}s）"
289:   fi
290: 
291:   echo
292:   echo "  完整日志: $LOG"
293:   exit 1
294: fi
295: 
296: # --------------------------------------------------------- 5. 可选挂回串口
297: 
298: # Put the line back to the console rate.  bk_loader left it at BAUD, and if
299: # that is not CONSOLE_BAUD then anything attaching afterwards -- screen, cat,
300: # minicom -- would see garbage and typing would do nothing.
301: if [ "$BAUD" != "$CONSOLE_BAUD" ]; then
302:   stty -F "$PORT" "$CONSOLE_BAUD" cs8 -cstopb -parenb raw -echo -crtscts \
303:     2>/dev/null
304:   echo "  串口已从 ${BAUD} 恢复为控制台的 ${CONSOLE_BAUD} baud"
305: fi
306: 
307: if [ "$ATTACH_SERIAL" -eq 1 ]; then
308:   echo
309:   echo "=== 挂上串口（Ctrl-A K 再按 y 退出，别用 Ctrl-A D）==="
310:   sleep 1
311:   exec screen "$PORT" "$CONSOLE_BAUD"
312: fi
313: 
314: echo
315: echo "  接串口看日志:  sg dialout -c \"screen $PORT $CONSOLE_BAUD\""

1: # BK7258 OpenVela AP移植
2: 
3: 本项目将OpenVela/NuttX移植到BK7258 AP核，并保留博通原厂CP固件、Bootloader、分区和最终打包流程。当前已实现AP核启动，以及AP日志通过Mailbox转发到CP UART0输出。
4: 
5: ## 简单使用说明
6: 
7: 本项目需要配合博通`bk_avdk_smp` SMP工程使用：
8: 
9: ```text
10: 工作区/
11: ├── contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/
12: └── bk_avdk_smp/
13: ```
14: 
15: 构建前，需要将比赛仓`external/bk_avdk_smp/`中的权威覆盖文件同步到
16: `bk_avdk_smp`。完整文件清单、可直接执行的同步脚本、逐字节校验、OpenVela AP
17: 构建、CP构建和最终固件打包步骤见`external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md`。Git协作和
18: 提交规则见`github开发指南.md`。
19: 
20: ## UART0控制台使用
21: 
22: 连接开发板UART0：
23: 
24: ```bash
25: picocom --no-escape -b 115200 --flow n --parity n --databits 8 /dev/ttyUSB0
26: ```
27: 
28: CP启动后可先查看AP链路状态，再进入AP的OpenVela NSH控制台：
29: 
30: ```text
31: ap_console status
32: ap_console open
33: ```
34: 
35: 进入AP控制台后可以直接执行NSH命令，例如：
36: 
37: ```text
38: help
39: uname -a
40: ps
41: free
42: ctrlc_test
43: ```
44: 
45: `ctrlc_test`会持续等待TTY `SIGINT`。按`Ctrl-C`后应打印
46: `ctrlc_test received SIGINT`并返回NSH提示符。
47: 
48: AP控制台支持方向键、Home、End、Delete、Backspace、命令历史，以及
49: `Ctrl-A`、`Ctrl-B`、`Ctrl-D`、`Ctrl-E`、`Ctrl-F`、`Ctrl-H`、`Ctrl-K`、
50: `Ctrl-L`、`Ctrl-N`、`Ctrl-P`和`Ctrl-U`等CLE快捷键。
51: 
52: 退出AP控制台并返回CP命令行时，严格按以下顺序操作：
53: 
54: 1. 按下`Ctrl-]`。
55: 2. 松开按键。
56: 3. 再按`.`。
57: 
58: 返回CP命令行后可再次检查状态：
59: 
60: ```text
61: ap_console status
62: ```
63: 
64: ## 主要目录
65: 
66: ```text
67: board/beken/chips/bk7258/                  BK7258 AP启动、中断、定时器和Mailbox驱动
68: board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/       BK7258 AP板级配置、链接脚本和bring-up
69: external/bk_avdk_smp/                      已验证的博通CP覆盖文件
70: logs/                                      AI Coding日志
71: ```
72: 
73: ## 已实现功能
74: 
75: - BK7258物理CPU1/AP启动OpenVela/NuttX。
76: - Cortex-M33启动向量、C运行时、MPU、FPU、IRQ和SysTick基础适配。
77: - Mailbox v2基础传输、logical channel、sequence、ACK、超时和FIFO full恢复。
78: - 原厂兼容HW_CTRL command 1 power-up、command 2两秒heartbeat，以及独立的PWC `0x5/0x11`生命周期握手。
79: - AP日志通过Mailbox UART0转发到CP物理UART0。
80: - GPIO40红灯和GPIO41绿灯由NuttX内核自动LED状态接口接管，用于显示
81:   中断、信号、断言、Panic、空闲和启动状态。
82: - AP、CP和Bootloader通过`bk_avdk_smp`标准打包流程生成`all-app.bin`。
83: - 当前为物理CPU1+CPU2的OpenVela/NuttX SMP，CP保持物理CPU0。
84:

87: # contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing
88: 
89: 👋 欢迎参加 **2026 首届 openvela AI 硬件开发者大赛**！
90: 
91: 这是组委会为你的队伍创建的**专属参赛仓库**（本仓为样例/模板，队伍编号 `264`；你看到的将是你自己的 `contest2026_<编号>_<队伍名>`）。比赛期间，你的全部参赛代码、打包产物与 AI Coding 日志都提交到这里。
92: 
93: > 本仓既是「代码仓」，又内置了一键拉取整套 openvela 工程的 `repo` 清单（manifest）。你只需跟它打交道，**自始至终只动一个文件夹**。
94: 
95: ---
96: 
97: ## 一、先读这些官方文档
98: 
99: **通用（所有赛道必读）：**
100: 
101: | 文档                                                                                                                                     | 用途                                           |
102: | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
103: | [《大赛总览》](https://github.com/open-vela/docs/blob/dev-ai-contest-2026/zh-cn/contest_2026/contest_overview.md)                        | 赛道、流程、评分、资源，建议先通读             |
104: | [《参赛代码提交指南》](https://github.com/open-vela/docs/blob/dev-ai-contest-2026/zh-cn/contest_2026/code_submission_guide.md)           | 仓库获取、提交流程、时间与权限（**以此为准**） |
105: | [《AI Coding 日志归集与提交手册》](https://github.com/open-vela/docs/blob/dev-ai-contest-2026/zh-cn/contest_2026/ai_coding_log_guide.md) | 如何导出 AI 对话日志并提交到 `logs/`           |
106: 
107: **按你的赛道选读（三选一）：**
108: 
109: | 赛道                  | 教程导航                                                                                                                                                 |
110: | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
111: | 快应用 / 手表应用创新 | [快应用教程导航](https://github.com/open-vela/docs/blob/dev-ai-contest-2026/zh-cn/contest_2026/quickapp/quickapp_guide_index.md)                         |
112: | AI 硬件产品创新       | [AI 硬件赛道教程导航](https://github.com/open-vela/docs/blob/dev-ai-contest-2026/zh-cn/contest_2026/ai_hardware/ai_hardware_guide_index.md)              |
113: | 新硬件适配            | [新硬件适配赛道教程导航](https://github.com/open-vela/docs/blob/dev-ai-contest-2026/zh-cn/contest_2026/hardware_porting/hardware_porting_guide_index.md) |
114:

116: 
117: ## 二、第一步：拉取完整工程
118: 
119: 用组委会提供的命令一键拉取「openvela 全量源码 + 你的专属仓」：
120: 
121: ```bash
122: repo init -u https://github.com/open-vela/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing \
123:   -b dev-ai-contest-2026 -m contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing.xml
124: repo sync -c -j8
125: ```
126: 
127: 同步后，你的整个仓库位于工作区的 `contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/`，openvela 全量源码在外层（`nuttx/`、`apps/`、`packages/`、`vendor/` 等）。
128: 
129: ---
130: 
131: ## 三、第二步：在哪里写代码
132: 
133: **只在自己的仓目录 `contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/` 里开发。** 不同作品形态放在对应子目录，manifest 会通过 `<linkfile>` 把它们**软链**到 openvela 编译树该在的位置——你不用手动 copy：
134: 
135: | 作品形态 | 你的代码放这里             | 系统自动映射到                                 |

66: static inline void nxsched_running_setpriority(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb,
67:                                                int sched_priority)
68: {
69:   FAR struct tcb_s *nxttcb;
70: 
71:   /* Get the TCB of the next highest priority, ready to run task */
72: 
73: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
74:   nxttcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_peek(list_readytorun());
75: #else
76:   nxttcb = tcb->flink;
77: #endif
78: 
79:   /* A context switch will occur if the new priority of the running
80:    * task becomes less than OR EQUAL TO the next highest priority
81:    * ready to run task.
82:    */
83: 
84: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
85: 
86:   /* A context switch will occur:
87:    * CASE 1. The new priority of the running task becomes less than or
88:    * equal to the next highest priority ready to run task.
89:    * CASE 2. In SMP, the affinity of tcb has changed and no longer includes
90:    * the current cpu.
91:    */
92: 
93:   if ((nxttcb && sched_priority <= nxttcb->sched_priority) ||
94:       (tcb->affinity & (1 << tcb->cpu)) == 0)
95: #else
96:   if (nxttcb && sched_priority <= nxttcb->sched_priority)
97: #endif
98:     {
99: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
100:       tcb->sched_priority = sched_priority;
101:       if (nxsched_deliver_task(this_cpu(), tcb->cpu, SWITCH_EQUAL))

103:           nxsched_switch(this_task(), tcb);
104:         }
105: #else
106:       FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
107: 
108:       if (rtcb->lockcount > 0)

114:            */

 #define MB_UART_PRIORITY      106

     {
       bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_UART_CREATE_ENTER);
-      ret = kthread_create("mb-uart0", MB_UART_BOOT_PRIORITY, 2048,
