526: static void mb_uart_channel_event(mb_uart_cb_t *chnl_cb, mb_chnl_event_t event)
527: {
528: 	if (event == MB_CHNL_EVENT_RX_ACK_SENT)
529: 	{
530: 		u8 peer = GET_DST_CPU_ID(chnl_cb->chnl_id);
531: 
532: 		if (!chnl_cb->tx_fence_req &&
533: 			bk_mailbox_ack_slots_used((mailbox_endpoint_t)peer) >=
534: 			MB_UART_ACK_FENCE_WATERMARK)
535: 		{
536: 			chnl_cb->tx_fence_req = 1;
537: 			chnl_cb->tx_state_req = 1;
538: 		}
539: 	}
540: 	else if (event == MB_CHNL_EVENT_ABORT_SENT)
541: 	{
542: 		chnl_cb->link_ready = 0;
543: 		chnl_cb->link_state = MB_UART_LINK_PROBING;
544: 		chnl_cb->probe_count = 0;
545: 		chnl_cb->probe_due_ms = rtos_get_time();
546: 		chnl_cb->tx_state_req = 1;
547: 	}
548: 	else if (event == MB_CHNL_EVENT_ABORT_FAILED)
549: 	{
550: 		chnl_cb->link_ready = 0;
551: 		chnl_cb->link_state = MB_UART_LINK_DOWN;
552: 		chnl_cb->tx_state_req = 0;
553: 		mb_uart_notify(chnl_cb, MB_UART_EVENT_DOWN);
554: 	}
555: 	else
556: 	{
557: 		if (chnl_cb->tx_inflight_len)
558: 		{
559: 			/* Delivery is unknowable after a lost ACK. Drop this chunk instead
560: 			 * of replaying terminal input and making duplicate commands. */
561: 			chnl_cb->tx_rd_idx = (chnl_cb->tx_rd_idx +
562: 					      chnl_cb->tx_inflight_len) %
563: 					     sizeof(chnl_cb->tx_buf);
564: 			chnl_cb->tx_inflight_len = 0;
565: 			chnl_cb->tx_retry = 0;
566: 			chnl_cb->status_error |= MB_UART_STATUS_TX_FAIL;
567: 		}
568: 		chnl_cb->link_ready = 0;
569: 		chnl_cb->probe_count = 0;
570: 		chnl_cb->probe_due_ms = rtos_get_time();
571: 		chnl_cb->link_state = event == MB_CHNL_EVENT_TX_TIMEOUT ?
572: 			MB_UART_LINK_ABORTING : MB_UART_LINK_PROBING;
573: 		chnl_cb->tx_state_req = event == MB_CHNL_EVENT_PEER_RESET;
574: 		if (event == MB_CHNL_EVENT_PEER_RESET)
575: 			mb_uart_notify(chnl_cb, MB_UART_EVENT_PEER_RESET);
576: 		else
577: 			mb_uart_notify(chnl_cb, MB_UART_EVENT_TIMEOUT);
578: 	}
579: 
580: 	if (chnl_cb->tx_isr_callback)
581: 		chnl_cb->tx_isr_callback(chnl_cb->tx_isr_param);
582: }

584: static bk_err_t mb_uart_init(mb_uart_cb_t *chnl_cb, u8 chnl_id)
585: {
586: 	bk_err_t		ret_code;
587: 
588: 	if(chnl_cb->chnl_inited)
589: 		return BK_OK;
590: 
591: 	memset(chnl_cb, 0, sizeof(mb_uart_cb_t));
592: 	chnl_cb->chnl_id = chnl_id;
593: 	chnl_cb->link_state = MB_UART_LINK_PROBING;
594: 	chnl_cb->tx_state_req = 1;
595: 
596: 	chnl_cb->tx_xchg_buff = mb_chnl_get_tx_buff(chnl_id);
597: 	chnl_cb->rx_xchg_buff = mb_chnl_get_rx_buff(chnl_id);
598: 
599: 	if( (chnl_cb->tx_xchg_buff == NULL) ||
600: 		(chnl_cb->rx_xchg_buff == NULL) )
601: 	{
602: 		return BK_FAIL;
603: 	}
604: 
605: 	ret_code = mb_chnl_open(chnl_id, chnl_cb);
606: 	if(ret_code != BK_OK)
607: 	{
608: 		return ret_code;
609: 	}
610: 
611: 	mb_chnl_ctrl(chnl_id, MB_CHNL_SET_RX_ISR, (void *)mb_uart_rx_isr);
612: 	mb_chnl_ctrl(chnl_id, MB_CHNL_SET_TX_CMPL_ISR, (void *)mb_uart_tx_cmpl_isr);
613: 	mb_chnl_ctrl(chnl_id, MB_CHNL_SET_TX_ISR, NULL);
614: 	mb_chnl_ctrl(chnl_id, MB_CHNL_SET_EVENT_ISR, (void *)mb_uart_channel_event);
615: 
616: 	chnl_cb->chnl_inited = 1;
617: 
618: 	return BK_OK;
619: }

621: static bk_err_t mb_uart_deinit(mb_uart_cb_t *chnl_cb, u8 chnl_id)
622: {
623: 	if(!chnl_cb->chnl_inited)
624: 		return BK_OK;
625: 
626: 	mb_chnl_ctrl(chnl_id, MB_CHNL_SET_RX_ISR, NULL);
627: 	mb_chnl_ctrl(chnl_id, MB_CHNL_SET_TX_CMPL_ISR, NULL);
628: 	mb_chnl_ctrl(chnl_id, MB_CHNL_SET_TX_ISR, NULL);
629: 	mb_chnl_ctrl(chnl_id, MB_CHNL_SET_EVENT_ISR, NULL);
630: 
631: 	mb_chnl_close(chnl_id);
632: 
633: 	chnl_cb->rx_isr_callback = NULL;
634: 	chnl_cb->tx_isr_callback = NULL;
635: 
636: 	chnl_cb->chnl_inited = 0;
637: 
638: 	return BK_OK;
639: }

641: static bk_err_t mb_uart_send_data(mb_uart_cb_t *chnl_cb)
642: {
643: 	bk_err_t	ret_val = BK_FAIL;
644: 
645: 	u16    rem_len, cpy_len;
646: 	u16    rd_idx, wr_idx;
647: 
648: 	if(chnl_cb->status_cts != 0)
649: 	{
650: 		return BK_ERR_BUSY;
651: 	}
652: 
653: 	rd_idx = chnl_cb->tx_rd_idx;
654: 	wr_idx = chnl_cb->tx_wr_idx;
655: 
656: 	if(rd_idx <= wr_idx)
657: 	{
658: 		cpy_len = wr_idx - rd_idx;
659: 	}
660: 	else
661: 	{
662: 		cpy_len = sizeof(chnl_cb->tx_buf) - (rd_idx - wr_idx);
663: 	}
664: 
665: 	if(cpy_len == 0)
666: 	{
667: 		return BK_FAIL;
668: 	}
669: 
670: 	if(cpy_len > MB_UART_TX_FIFO_LEN)
671: 	{
672: 		cpy_len = MB_UART_TX_FIFO_LEN;
673: 	}
674: 
675: 	if(rd_idx < wr_idx)
676: 	{
677: 		memcpy(chnl_cb->tx_xchg_buff, chnl_cb->tx_buf + rd_idx, cpy_len);
678: 	}
679: 	else
680: 	{
681: 		rem_len = sizeof(chnl_cb->tx_buf) - rd_idx;
682: 
683: 		if(rem_len >= cpy_len)
684: 		{
685: 			memcpy(chnl_cb->tx_xchg_buff, chnl_cb->tx_buf + rd_idx, cpy_len);
686: 		}
687: 		else
688: 		{
689: 			memcpy(chnl_cb->tx_xchg_buff, chnl_cb->tx_buf + rd_idx, rem_len);
690: 
691: 			memcpy(chnl_cb->tx_xchg_buff + rem_len, chnl_cb->tx_buf, cpy_len - rem_len);
692: 		}
693: 	}
694: 
695: 	chnl_cb->tx_cmd = MB_UART_SEND_DATA;
696: 
697: 	mb_uart_cmd_t	uart_cmd;
698: 
699: 	memset(&uart_cmd, 0, sizeof(uart_cmd));
700: 	uart_cmd.chnl_hdr.cmd  = MB_UART_SEND_DATA;
701: 	uart_cmd.cmd_buff      = (void *)(chnl_cb->tx_xchg_buff);
702: 	uart_cmd.cmd_data_len  = cpy_len;
703: 	uart_cmd.uart_rts      = chnl_cb->ctrl_rts;
704: 	uart_cmd.resvd         = 0;
705: 	uart_cmd.crc8          = cal_crc8_0x31(chnl_cb->tx_xchg_buff, cpy_len);
706: 
707: 	ret_val = mb_chnl_write(chnl_cb->chnl_id, (mb_chnl_cmd_t *)&uart_cmd);
708: 
709: 	if(ret_val == BK_OK)
710: 	{
711: 		chnl_cb->tx_inflight_len = cpy_len;
712: 	}
713: 
714: 	return ret_val;
715: }

791: static u16 mb_uart_write_data(mb_uart_cb_t *chnl_cb, u8 * data_buf, u16 data_len)
792: {
793: 	u16    rem_len, wr_len;
794: 	u16    rd_idx, wr_idx;
795: 
796: 	rd_idx = chnl_cb->tx_rd_idx;
797: 	wr_idx = chnl_cb->tx_wr_idx;
798: 
799: 	if(rd_idx > wr_idx)
800: 	{
801: 		rem_len = rd_idx - wr_idx - 1;  // always reserved one byte space.
802: 	}
803: 	else
804: 	{
805: 		rem_len = sizeof(chnl_cb->tx_buf) - (wr_idx - rd_idx) - 1;
806: 	}
807: 
808: 	wr_len = data_len;
809: 	if(wr_len > rem_len)
810: 		wr_len = rem_len;
811: 
812: 	if(wr_idx < rd_idx)
813: 	{
814: 		memcpy(chnl_cb->tx_buf + wr_idx, data_buf, wr_len);
815: 	}
816: 	else
817: 	{
818: 		if(rd_idx != 0)
819: 			rem_len = sizeof(chnl_cb->tx_buf) - wr_idx;  // if rx_idx == 0, reserved one byte at tail of the array.
820: 
821: 		if(rem_len >= wr_len)
822: 		{
823: 			memcpy(chnl_cb->tx_buf + wr_idx, data_buf, wr_len);
824: 		}
825: 		else
826: 		{
827: 			memcpy(chnl_cb->tx_buf + wr_idx, data_buf, rem_len);
828: 
829: 			memcpy(chnl_cb->tx_buf, data_buf + rem_len, wr_len - rem_len);
830: 		}
831: 	}
832: 
833: 	chnl_cb->tx_wr_idx = (wr_idx + wr_len) % sizeof(chnl_cb->tx_buf);
834: 
835: 	/* trigger send! */
836: 	mb_uart_send_data_trigger(chnl_cb);
837: 
838: 	return wr_len;
839: }

841: static u16 mb_uart_read_data(mb_uart_cb_t *chnl_cb, u8 * data_buf, u16 buf_len)
842: {
843: 	u16    rem_len, rd_len;
844: 
845: 	if(!chnl_cb->chnl_inited)
846: 		return 0;
847: 
848: 	u16    rd_idx, wr_idx, data_cnt;
849: 
850: 	rd_idx = chnl_cb->rx_rd_idx;
851: 	wr_idx = chnl_cb->rx_wr_idx;
852: 
853: 	if(rd_idx <= wr_idx)
854: 	{
855: 		data_cnt = wr_idx - rd_idx;
856: 	}
857: 	else
858: 	{
859: 		data_cnt = sizeof(chnl_cb->rx_buf) - (rd_idx - wr_idx);
860: 	}
861: 
862: 	rd_len = data_cnt;
863: 	if(rd_len > buf_len)
864: 		rd_len = buf_len;
865: 
866: 	if(rd_len == 0)
867: 	{
868: 		return 0;
869: 	}
870: 
871: 	if(rd_idx < wr_idx)
872: 	{
873: 		memcpy(data_buf, chnl_cb->rx_buf + rd_idx, rd_len);
874: 		chnl_cb->rx_rd_idx += rd_len;
875: 	}
876: 	else
877: 	{
878: 		rem_len = sizeof(chnl_cb->rx_buf) - rd_idx;
879: 
880: 		if(rem_len > rd_len)
881: 		{
882: 			memcpy(data_buf, chnl_cb->rx_buf + rd_idx, rd_len);
883: 			chnl_cb->rx_rd_idx += rd_len;
884: 		}
885: 		else
886: 		{
887: 			memcpy(data_buf, chnl_cb->rx_buf + rd_idx, rem_len);
888: 			if(rem_len < rd_len)
889: 			{
890: 				memcpy(data_buf + rem_len, chnl_cb->rx_buf, rd_len - rem_len);
891: 			}
892: 
893: 			chnl_cb->rx_rd_idx = rd_len - rem_len;
894: 		}
895: 	}
896: 
897: 	data_cnt -= rd_len;
898: 
899: 	/* rts assert...... */
900: 	if(data_cnt < ((sizeof(chnl_cb->rx_buf) - 1 - MB_UART_RX_FIFO_LEN) * 8 / 10))
901: 	{
902: 		if( chnl_cb->ctrl_rts != 0)
903: 		{
904: 			chnl_cb->ctrl_rts = 0;
905: 			mb_uart_send_state_trigger(chnl_cb);
906: 		}
907: 	}
908: 
909: 	return rd_len;
910: 
911: }

997: 	if (id >= MB_UART_MAX || !mb_uart_cb[id].chnl_inited)

999: 
1000: 	mb_chnl_poll();
1001: 	if (mb_uart_cb[id].link_state == MB_UART_LINK_DOWN &&
1002: 		!mb_uart_cb[id].tx_in_process &&
1003: 		(int32_t)(rtos_get_time() - mb_uart_cb[id].probe_due_ms) >= 0)
1004: 	{

1006: 		mb_uart_cb[id].link_state = MB_UART_LINK_PROBING;
1007: 		mb_uart_cb[id].tx_state_req = 1;
1008: 	}
1009: 	if (!mb_uart_cb[id].tx_in_process && mb_uart_cb[id].tx_state_req)
1010: 	{
1011: 		if (mb_uart_cb[id].link_state == MB_UART_LINK_PROBING &&
1012: 			(int32_t)(rtos_get_time() - mb_uart_cb[id].probe_due_ms) < 0)
1013: 			return;
1014: 		if (mb_uart_cb[id].probe_count >= MB_UART_PROBE_MAX)
1015: 		{
1016: 			mb_uart_cb[id].tx_state_req = 0;
1017: 			mb_uart_cb[id].link_state = MB_UART_LINK_DOWN;
1018: 			mb_uart_cb[id].probe_due_ms = rtos_get_time() +
1019: 				MB_UART_DOWN_RETRY_MS;
1020: 			return;
1021: 		}
1022: 		if (mb_uart_send_state_trigger(&mb_uart_cb[id]) == BK_OK)
1023: 		{
1024: 			mb_uart_cb[id].tx_state_req = 0;
1025: 			mb_uart_cb[id].probe_count++;
1026: 			if (!mb_uart_cb[id].link_ready)

234: static void mb_chnl_ack_retry(void)
235: {
236: 	u16 chnl_type = MB_PHY_ACK_CHNL;
237: 
238: 	while (1)
239: 	{
240: 		mb_ack_entry_t entry;
241: 		bk_err_t ret;
242: 		u32 flags = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
243: 
244: 		if (!ack_count || ack_sending)
245: 		{
246: 			mb_chnl_exit_critical(flags);
247: 			return;
248: 		}
249: 		entry = ack_queue[ack_read];
250: 		ack_sending = 1;
251: 		mb_chnl_exit_critical(flags);
252: 
253: 		ret = bk_mailbox_send_safe(&entry.data, SELF_CPU,
254: 			(mailbox_endpoint_t)entry.destination, &chnl_type);
255: 		flags = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
256: 		if (ret != BK_OK)
257: 		{
258: 			phy_chnl_x_cb[entry.destination].ack_retry_cnt++;
259: 			ack_sending = 0;
260: 			mb_chnl_exit_critical(flags);
261: 			return;
262: 		}
263: 		ack_read = (ack_read + 1) % MB_ACK_QUEUE_LEN;
264: 		ack_count--;
265: 		ack_sending = 0;
266: 		mb_chnl_exit_critical(flags);
267: 		s_mailbox_rx_ack_cnt++;
268: 		mb_chnl_notify((mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[entry.destination],
269: 			phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[entry.destination],
270: 			MB_CHNL_EVENT_RX_ACK_SENT);
271: 	}

274: static bool mb_chnl_ack_enqueue(u8 destination, const mailbox_data_t *data)

277: 	mb_ack_entry_t *entry;

280: 	{
281: 		phy_chnl_x_cb[destination].ack_queue_full_cnt++;
282: 		mb_chnl_exit_critical(flags);
283: 		return false;
284: 	}
285: 	entry = &ack_queue[ack_write];
286: 	entry->data = *data;
287: 	entry->destination = destination;
288: 	ack_write = (ack_write + 1) % MB_ACK_QUEUE_LEN;
289: 	ack_count++;
290: 	mb_chnl_exit_critical(flags);
291: 	mb_chnl_ack_retry();

351: 	if(SELF_CPU != GET_SRC_CPU_ID(log_chnl))

356: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
357: 
358: 	if(phy_chnl_idx >= PHY_CHNL_NUM)
359: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;

365: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
366: 
367: 	phy_chnl_ptr->tx_seq++;
368: 	phy_chnl_ptr->tx_log_chnl = log_chnl;
369: 
370: 	cmd_ptr = (mb_phy_chnl_cmd_t *)&log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].chnnl_tx_buff;
371: 
372: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl = log_chnl;

374: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.ctrl  = 0;
375: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.state = 0;
376: 
377: 	phy_chnl_ptr->tx_hdr_cmd = cmd_ptr->hdr.cmd;
378: 	phy_chnl_ptr->last_cmd_header = cmd_ptr->hdr.data;
379: 
380: 	phy_chnl_ptr->param1 = cmd_ptr->param1;
381: 	phy_chnl_ptr->param2 = cmd_ptr->param2;
382: 	phy_chnl_ptr->param3 = cmd_ptr->param3;

384: 	__DMB();

387: 	mailbox_endpoint_t    dst_cpu = (mailbox_endpoint_t)(phy_chnl_idx);
388: 
389: 	ret_code = bk_mailbox_send(&log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].chnnl_tx_buff, SELF_CPU, dst_cpu, (void *)&chnl_type);
390: 
391: 	if(ret_code != BK_OK)
392: 	{
393: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_fault_cnt++;
394: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_fault_cnt |= 0x40000000;
395: 
396: 		return ret_code;
397: 	}
398: 
399: 	s_mailbox_tx_cnt++;

401: 	log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_state = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
402: 
403: 	if(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_isr != NULL)
404: 	{
405: 		log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_isr(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].isr_param);  	/* phy_chnl is BUSY now, tx_isr will not trigger phy_chnl_start_tx. */
406: 	}

408: 	return BK_OK;

418: 	mb_phy_chnl_cb_t * phy_chnl_ptr;
419: 	mb_log_chnl_cb_t * log_chnl_cb_x;
420: 
421: 	log_chnl = ack_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl;
422: 	if (ack_ptr->hdr.ctrl & CHNL_CTRL_RESET)
423: 	{
424: 		mb_chnl_ack_t failure;
425: 
426: 		phy_chnl_idx = GET_SRC_CPU_ID(log_chnl);
427: 		if (ack_ptr->hdr.ctrl != (CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX | CHNL_CTRL_RESET) ||
428: 			ack_ptr->hdr.state != 0 || ack_ptr->hdr.cmd != 0 ||
429: 			ack_ptr->hdr.tx_seq != 0 || ack_ptr->data1 != 0 ||
430: 			ack_ptr->data2 != 0 || ack_ptr->data3 != 0 ||
431: 			GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl) != SELF_CPU ||
432: 			phy_chnl_idx == SELF_CPU || phy_chnl_idx >= PHY_CHNL_NUM)
433: 		{
434: 			s_mailbox_tx_ack_fault_mask |= 0x10;
435: 			if (phy_chnl_idx < PHY_CHNL_NUM)
436: 				phy_chnl_x_cb[phy_chnl_idx].reset_bad_cnt++;
437: 			return;
438: 		}
439: 
440: 		phy_chnl_ptr = &phy_chnl_x_cb[phy_chnl_idx];
441: 		phy_chnl_ptr->recovering = 1;
442: 		log_chnl_cb_x = (mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[phy_chnl_idx];
443: 		mb_chnl_notify(log_chnl_cb_x,
444: 				   phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx],
445: 				   MB_CHNL_EVENT_PEER_RESET);
446: 		u32 reset_flags = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
447: 		if (phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state == CHNL_STATE_BUSY)
448: 		{
449: 			phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
450: 			phy_chnl_ptr->busy_since_ms = 0;
451: 			mb_chnl_exit_critical(reset_flags);
452: 			log_chnl_idx = GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(phy_chnl_ptr->tx_log_chnl);
453: 			if (log_chnl_idx < phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx] &&
454: 				log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_cmpl_isr)
455: 			{
456: 				memset(&failure, 0, sizeof(failure));
457: 				failure.hdr.cmd = phy_chnl_ptr->tx_hdr_cmd;
458: 				failure.hdr.state = CHNL_STATE_COM_FAIL;
459: 				log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_cmpl_isr(
460: 					log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].isr_param, &failure);
461: 			}
462: 			bk_mailbox_tx_timeout((mailbox_endpoint_t)phy_chnl_idx);
463: 		}
464: 		else
465: 			mb_chnl_exit_critical(reset_flags);
466: 		mb_chnl_fail_pending(log_chnl_cb_x,
467: 				     phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx]);
468: 		return;
469: 	}
470: 
471: 	phy_chnl_idx = GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl);   // = DST_CPU_ID;
472: 	log_chnl_idx = GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(log_chnl);
473: 
474: 	s_mailbox_tx_ack_cnt++;
475: 
476: 	if(SELF_CPU != GET_SRC_CPU_ID(log_chnl)) {
477: 		s_mailbox_tx_ack_fault_mask |= 0x1;
478: 		return;
479: 	}
480: 
481: 
482: 	if(SELF_CPU == phy_chnl_idx)  // received from self.
483: 	{
484: 		s_mailbox_tx_ack_fault_mask |= 0x2;
485: 		return;
486: 	}
487: 
488: 
489: 	if(phy_chnl_idx >= PHY_CHNL_NUM){
490: 		s_mailbox_tx_ack_fault_mask |= 0x4;
491: 		return;
492: 	}
493: 
494: 	phy_chnl_ptr = &phy_chnl_x_cb[phy_chnl_idx];
495: 	phy_chnl_ptr->last_ack_header = ack_ptr->hdr.data;
496: 	phy_chnl_ptr->last_ack_data1 = ack_ptr->data1;
497: 	log_chnl_cb_x = (mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)(phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[phy_chnl_idx]);
498: 
499: 	if(log_chnl_idx >= phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx])
500: 	{
501: 		s_mailbox_tx_ack_fault_mask |= 0x8;
502: 		return;
503: 	}
504: 
505: 	u32 claim_flags = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
506: 	if (phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state != CHNL_STATE_BUSY ||
507: 		(ack_ptr->hdr.ctrl != CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX) ||
508: 		 (ack_ptr->hdr.state & ~CHNL_STATE_COM_FAIL) ||
509: 		 (log_chnl != phy_chnl_ptr->tx_log_chnl) ||
510: 		 (ack_ptr->hdr.tx_seq != phy_chnl_ptr->tx_seq) ||
511: 		 (ack_ptr->hdr.cmd != phy_chnl_ptr->tx_hdr_cmd))
512: 	{
513: 		phy_chnl_ptr->rx_fault_cnt++;
514: 		phy_chnl_ptr->rx_fault_cnt |= 0x40000000;
515: 		mb_chnl_exit_critical(claim_flags);
516: 		return;
517: 	}
518: 	phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
519: 	phy_chnl_ptr->busy_since_ms = 0;
520: 	mb_chnl_exit_critical(claim_flags);
521: 
522: 	bk_mailbox_tx_complete((mailbox_endpoint_t)phy_chnl_idx);
523: 
524: 	if(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_cmpl_isr != NULL)
525: 	{
526: 		/* clear following header members. */
527: 		ack_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl = 0;
528: 		ack_ptr->hdr.tx_seq       = 0;
529: 		ack_ptr->hdr.ctrl         = 0;
530: 
531: 		/* hdr.state, hdr.cmd these 2 members keep untouched. */
532: 		s_mailbox_tx_compl_cnt++;
533: 		log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_cmpl_isr(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].isr_param, (mb_chnl_ack_t *)ack_ptr);
534: 	} else {
535: 		s_mailbox_tx_ack_fault_mask |= 0x100;
536: 	}
537: 
538: 	u32 int_mask = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
539: 	if (phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state != CHNL_STATE_IDLE)
540: 	{
541: 		mb_chnl_exit_critical(int_mask);
542: 		return;
543: 	}
544: 	for(log_chnl_idx = 0; log_chnl_idx < phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx]; log_chnl_idx++)  /* priority descended search. */
545: 	{
546: 		if(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_state != CHNL_STATE_IDLE)
547: 			break;
548: 	}
549: 
550: 	if(log_chnl_idx >= phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx])
551: 	{
552: 		mb_chnl_exit_critical(int_mask);
553: 		return;
554: 	}
555: 
556: 	log_chnl = CPX_LOG_CHNL_START(SELF_CPU, phy_chnl_idx) + log_chnl_idx;
557: 
558: 	/* About to dispatch the next pending tx on this physical channel:
559: 	 * refresh the busy-watchdog timestamp so its lifetime starts from
560: 	 * here rather than carrying over from the previous transaction. */
561: 	phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state = CHNL_STATE_BUSY;
562: 	phy_chnl_ptr->busy_since_ms = rtos_get_time();
563: 
564: 	ret_code = mb_phy_chnl_tx_cmd(log_chnl);
565: 
566: 	if(ret_code != BK_OK)
567: 	{
568: 		log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_state = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
569: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state               = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
570: 		phy_chnl_ptr->busy_since_ms          = 0;
571: 	}
572: 	mb_chnl_exit_critical(int_mask);
573: 
574: 	return;
575: 
576: }

578: static void mb_phy_chnl_rx_cmd_isr(mb_phy_chnl_cmd_t *cmd_ptr)
579: {
580: 	phy_chnnl_hdr_t  chnl_hdr;
581: 	u8			log_chnl = cmd_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl;
582: 
583: 	u8		phy_chnl_idx;
584: 	u8		log_chnl_idx;
585: 
586: 	mb_phy_chnl_cb_t * phy_chnl_ptr;
587: 	mb_log_chnl_cb_t * log_chnl_cb_x;
588: 
589: 	phy_chnl_idx = GET_SRC_CPU_ID(log_chnl);   // = SRC_CPU_ID; from SRC_CPU.
590: 	log_chnl_idx = GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(log_chnl);
591: 
592: 	s_mailbox_rx_cnt++;
593: 
594: 	if(SELF_CPU != GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl))
595: 		return;
596: 
597: 	if(SELF_CPU == phy_chnl_idx)  // received from self.
598: 		return;
599: 
600: 	if(phy_chnl_idx >= PHY_CHNL_NUM)
601: 		return;
602: 
603: 	phy_chnl_ptr = &phy_chnl_x_cb[phy_chnl_idx];
604: 	log_chnl_cb_x = (mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)(phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[phy_chnl_idx]);
605: 
606: 	chnl_hdr.data = cmd_ptr->hdr.data;
607: 
608: 	if(log_chnl_idx >= phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx])
609: 	{
610: 		phy_chnl_ptr->rx_fault_cnt++;
611: 		phy_chnl_ptr->rx_fault_cnt |= 0x80000000;
612: 
613: 		return;
614: 	}
615: 
616: 	if(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].rx_status_isr != NULL)
617: 	{
618: 		/* clear all other hdr members except hdr.cmd. */
619: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl = 0;
620: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.tx_seq       = 0;
621: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.ctrl         = 0;
622: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.state        = 0;
623: 
624: 		if (log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].rx_status_isr(
625: 			log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].isr_param,
626: 			(mb_chnl_cmd_t *)cmd_ptr) != BK_OK)
627: 			chnl_hdr.state |= CHNL_STATE_COM_FAIL;
628: 	}
629: 	else if(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].rx_isr != NULL)
630: 	{
631: 		/* clear all other hdr members except hdr.cmd. */
632: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl = 0;
633: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.tx_seq       = 0;
634: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.ctrl         = 0;
635: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.state        = 0;
636: 
637: 		log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].rx_isr(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].isr_param, (mb_chnl_cmd_t *)cmd_ptr);
638: 
639: 		/* !!!! cmd_ptr buffer now contains ACK data !!!!. */
640: 	}
641: 	else
642: 	{
643: 		memset(cmd_ptr, 0, sizeof(*cmd_ptr));
644: 		cmd_ptr->hdr.data = chnl_hdr.data;
645: 		chnl_hdr.state |= CHNL_STATE_COM_FAIL;		/* cmd NO target app, it is an ACK bit to peer CPU. */
646: 	}
647: 
648: 	if(chnl_hdr.ctrl & CHNL_CTRL_SYNC_TX)
649: 	{
650: 		/* sync tx cmd, do NOT send ACK. */
651: 		return;
652: 	}
653: 
654: 	/* RE-USE the copied command buffer to construct the stable ACK. */
655: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.data  = chnl_hdr.data;
656: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.ctrl |= CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX;			/* ACK msg, use the ACK channel.  */
657: 
658: 	if (!mb_chnl_ack_enqueue(phy_chnl_idx, (mailbox_data_t *)cmd_ptr))
659: 	{
660: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_fault_cnt++;
661: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_fault_cnt |= 0x80000000;
662: 		return;
663: 	}
664: 	return;
665: }

667: static void mb_phy_chnl_rx_isr(mailbox_data_t * mb_data)
668: {
669: 	mb_phy_chnl_union_t	rx_data;
670: 
671: 	rx_data.mb_data.param0 = mb_data->param0;
672: 	rx_data.mb_data.param1 = mb_data->param1;
673: 	rx_data.mb_data.param2 = mb_data->param2;
674: 	rx_data.mb_data.param3 = mb_data->param3;
675: 	/* the following process will damage the input parameter,
676: 	so pass in the pointer of copied parameter instad of the original. */
677: 
678: 	/*
679: 	 *  there are 2 boxes in one MAILBOXn HW,
680: 	 *  but no way to know which box this msg is from in current mailbox_driver design.
681: 	 *  so use the CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX bit in the msg hdr.ctrl to distinguish where it is from.
682: 	 *  when CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX is set, it means from ack box ( MAILBOXn_BOX1 ).
683: 	 */
684: 	if(rx_data.phy_ch_hdr.ctrl & CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX)		/* rx ack. */
685: 	{
686: 		mb_phy_chnl_rx_ack_isr(&rx_data.phy_ch_ack);
687: 	}
688: 	else		/* rx cmd. */
689: 	{
690: 		mb_phy_chnl_rx_cmd_isr(&rx_data.phy_ch_cmd);
691: 	}
692: }

694: static bk_err_t mb_phy_chnl_start_tx(u8 log_chnl)
695: {
696: 	bk_err_t	ret_code;
697: 
698: 	u8		phy_chnl_idx;
699: 
700: 	mb_phy_chnl_cb_t * phy_chnl_ptr;
701: 
702: 	phy_chnl_idx = GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl);   // = DST_CPU_ID;
703: 
704: 	if(SELF_CPU == phy_chnl_idx)  // transferred to self.
705: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
706: 
707: 	if(phy_chnl_idx >= PHY_CHNL_NUM)
708: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
709: 
710: 	phy_chnl_ptr = &phy_chnl_x_cb[phy_chnl_idx];
711: 
712: 	if(phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state == CHNL_STATE_IDLE)
713: 	{
714: 		phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state = CHNL_STATE_BUSY;		/* MUST set channel state to BUSY firstly. */
715: 		phy_chnl_ptr->busy_since_ms = rtos_get_time();
716: 		/* start_tx->tx_cmd->tx_isr callback->mb_chnl_write->start_tx, it is a loop.
717: 		   break the loop by setting the phy_chnl_cb.tx_state to busy. */
718: 
719: 		ret_code = mb_phy_chnl_tx_cmd(log_chnl);
720: 
721: 		if(ret_code != BK_OK)
722: 		{
723: 			/* tx_cmd failed before the data hit hardware: roll back BOTH
724: 			 * physical and logical state, so the caller can retry and so
725: 			 * the logical channel does not stay BUSY forever. */
726: 			u8                   log_chnl_idx_fail = GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(log_chnl);
727: 			mb_log_chnl_cb_t    *log_chnl_cb_x_fail =
728: 				(mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)(phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[phy_chnl_idx]);
729: 
730: 			if (log_chnl_idx_fail < phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_chnl_idx]) {
731: 				log_chnl_cb_x_fail[log_chnl_idx_fail].tx_state = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
732: 			}
733: 			phy_chnl_ptr->tx_state = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
734: 			phy_chnl_ptr->busy_since_ms = 0;
735: 			return ret_code;
736: 		}
737: 	}
738: 
739: 	return BK_OK;
740: }

742: volatile uint32_t s_mailbox_sync_cnt = 0;
743: 
744: static bk_err_t mb_phy_chnl_tx_cmd_sync(u8 log_chnl, mb_phy_chnl_cmd_t *cmd_ptr)
745: {
746: 	bk_err_t		ret_code;
747: 	u16 			chnl_type;
748: 
749: 	u8		phy_chnl_idx;
750: 
751: 	phy_chnl_idx = GET_DST_CPU_ID(log_chnl);   // = DST_CPU_ID;
752: 
753: #if !CONFIG_SOC_SMP
754: 	if(SELF_CPU != GET_SRC_CPU_ID(log_chnl))
755: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
756: #endif
757: 
758: 	if(SELF_CPU == phy_chnl_idx)  // transferred to self.
759: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
760: 
761: 	if(phy_chnl_idx >= PHY_CHNL_NUM)
762: 		return BK_ERR_PARAM;
763: 
764: 	mailbox_endpoint_t    dst_cpu = (mailbox_endpoint_t)(phy_chnl_idx);
765: 
766: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.logical_chnl = log_chnl;
767: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.tx_seq = 0;
768: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.ctrl  = CHNL_CTRL_SYNC_TX;
769: 	cmd_ptr->hdr.state = 0;
770: 
771: 	chnl_type = MB_PHY_CMD_CHNL;
772: 
773: 	s_mailbox_sync_cnt++;
774: 
775: 	/*
776: 	 * can't wait 'phy_chnl_cb.tx_state' to be CHNL_STATE_IDLE here,
777: 	 * 'phy_chnl_cb.tx_state' is set to CHNL_STATE_IDLE in interrupt callback.
778: 	 * but the interrupt may be disabled when this API is called.
779: 	 *    wait physical channel HW to be IDLE by <POLLing> !!
780: 	 */
781: 	while(1)
782: 	{
783: 		ret_code = bk_mailbox_send_safe((mailbox_data_t *)cmd_ptr, SELF_CPU, dst_cpu, (void *)&chnl_type);
784: 
785: 		if(ret_code != BK_ERR_MAILBOX_TIMEOUT)
786: 		{
787: 			break;
788: 		}
789: 	}
790: 
791: 	return ret_code;
792: }

795: /* =====================      logical channel APIs      ==================*/
796: /*
797:   * init logical chnanel module.
798:   * return:
799:   *     succeed: BK_OK;
800:   *     failed  : fail code.
801:   *
802:   */
803: bk_err_t mb_chnl_init(void)
804: {
805: 	bk_err_t		ret_code;
806: 	int				i, j;
807: 
808: 	mb_log_chnl_cb_t * log_chnl_cb_x;
809: 
810: 	/*
811: 	 * mb_chnl_init() is reached from mb_chnl_open(), which is called by
812: 	 * many subsystems (shell log forwarding, ipc_init, mb_uart, ...).
813: 	 * Each one of those callers runs on its own FreeRTOS task and they
814: 	 * can race here:
815: 	 *
816: 	 *   Task A: enters mb_chnl_open(MB_CHNL_LOG), sees mb_chnnl_init_ok==0,
817: 	 *           enters mb_chnl_init(), runs all the memset's, sets
818: 	 *           mb_chnnl_init_ok=1, returns. Caller then sets
819: 	 *           log_chnl_cb2[15].in_used=1 and installs rx_isr.
820: 	 *   Task B (preempted in the middle of mb_chnl_open before the
821: 	 *           init_ok check finishes): comes back, sees init_ok still
822: 	 *           == 0 (because it sampled before A set it), enters
823: 	 *           mb_chnl_init() AGAIN, and the memset wipes the
824: 	 *           log_chnl_cb_x[] array that A just populated.
825: 	 *
826: 	 * Fix: serialize the body with the existing critical section so the
827: 	 * "if (init_ok) return; ... init_ok = 1;" sequence is atomic w.r.t.
828: 	 * other tasks. The double-check pattern still keeps the fast path
829: 	 * lock-free once init has completed.
830: 	 */
831: 	if(mb_chnnl_init_ok)
832: 	{
833: 		return BK_OK;
834: 	}
835: 
836: 	uint32_t init_int_mask = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
837: 	if(mb_chnnl_init_ok)
838: 	{
839: 		mb_chnl_exit_critical(init_int_mask);
840: 		return BK_OK;
841: 	}
842: 
843: 	memset(&phy_chnl_x_cb, 0, sizeof(phy_chnl_x_cb));
844: 	memset(ack_queue, 0, sizeof(ack_queue));
845: 	ack_read = 0;
846: 	ack_write = 0;
847: 	ack_count = 0;
848: 	ack_sending = 0;
849: 	for(i = 0; i < PHY_CHNL_NUM; i++)
850: 	{
851: 		phy_chnl_x_cb[i].tx_state = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
852: 
853: 		log_chnl_cb_x = (mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)(phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[i]);
854: 
855: 		memset(log_chnl_cb_x, 0, sizeof(mb_log_chnl_cb_t) * phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[i]);
856: 
857: 		for(j = 0; j < phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[i]; j++)
858: 		{
859: 			log_chnl_cb_x[j].tx_state = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
860: 		}
861: 	}
862: 
863: 	ret_code = bk_mailbox_init();
864: 	if(ret_code != BK_OK)
865: 	{
866: 		mb_chnl_exit_critical(init_int_mask);
867: 		return ret_code;
868: 	}
869: 
870: 	mailbox_endpoint_t    dst_cpu;
871: 
872: 	for(i = 0; i < PHY_CHNL_NUM; i++)
873: 	{
874: 		dst_cpu = (mailbox_endpoint_t)(i);  // dst_cpu_id;
875: 
876: 		bk_mailbox_recv_callback_register(dst_cpu, SELF_CPU, mb_phy_chnl_rx_isr);
877: 	}
878: 
879: 	mb_chnnl_init_ok = 1;
880: 	bk_mailbox_rx_ready_callback_register(mb_chnl_rx_ready);
881: 
882: 	mb_chnl_exit_critical(init_int_mask);
883: 
884: 	return BK_OK;
885: }

887: /*
888:   * open logical chnanel.
889:   * input:
890:   *     log_chnl  : logical channel id to open.
891:   *     callback_param : param passsed to all callbacks.
892:   * return:
893:   *     succeed: BK_OK;
894:   *     failed  : fail code.
895:   *
896:   */
897: bk_err_t mb_chnl_open(u8 log_chnl, void * callback_param)
898: {
899: 	if(!mb_chnnl_init_ok)	/* if driver is not initialized. */
900: 	{
901: 		bk_err_t		ret_code;
902: 
903: 		ret_code = mb_chnl_init();
904: 
905: 		if(ret_code != BK_OK)
906: 		{
907: 			return ret_code;
908: 		}
909: 	}

1035: 		return BK_ERR_STATE;

1038: 	mb_phy_chnl_cb_t *phy = &phy_chnl_x_cb[phy_chnl_idx];
1039: 	mb_chnl_cmd_t *logical_cmd = cmd_buf;

1041: 	if (phy->recovering &&
1042: 		!(log_chnl == MB_CHNL_UART0 &&
1043: 		  logical_cmd->hdr.cmd == MB_UART_STATE_COMMAND))
1044: 	{
1045: 		mb_chnl_exit_critical(int_mask);
1046: 		return BK_ERR_BUSY;
1047: 	}
1048: 
1049: 	if(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_state != CHNL_STATE_IDLE)
1050: 	{
1051: 		mb_chnl_exit_critical(int_mask);
1052: 
1053: 		return BK_ERR_BUSY;
1054: 	}
1055: 
1056: 	write_len = sizeof(mailbox_data_t) > sizeof(mb_chnl_cmd_t) ? sizeof(mb_chnl_cmd_t) : sizeof(mailbox_data_t);
1057: 
1058: 	memset(&log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].chnnl_tx_buff, 0,
1059: 	       sizeof(log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].chnnl_tx_buff));
1060: 	memcpy(&log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].chnnl_tx_buff, cmd_buf, write_len);

1062: 	/* set to BUSY means there is data in tx-buff. mb_phy_chnl_rx_ack_isr will get it to send. */
1063: 	log_chnl_cb_x[log_chnl_idx].tx_state = CHNL_STATE_BUSY;   /* MUST set to BUSY after data was copied. */
1064: 	__DMB();
1065: 
1066: 	bk_err_t start_ret = mb_phy_chnl_start_tx(log_chnl);
1067: 
1068: 	mb_chnl_exit_critical(int_mask);
1069: 
1070: 	return start_ret;

1089: 	u8		log_chnl_idx = GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(log_chnl);

1158: void mb_chnl_poll(void)
1159: {
1160: 	u8 phy_idx;
1161: 	u32 poll_flags = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
1162: 
1163: 	/* The CPU1 boot transaction may poll directly while ap_console is also
1164: 	 * scheduled.  Serialize the whole poll pass without holding the channel
1165: 	 * lock across callbacks and physical sends.
1166: 	 */
1167: 	if (s_poll_active)
1168: 	{
1169: 		mb_chnl_exit_critical(poll_flags);
1170: 		return;
1171: 	}
1172: 	s_poll_active = 1;
1173: 	mb_chnl_exit_critical(poll_flags);
1174: 
1175: 	bk_mailbox_poll();
1176: 	mb_chnl_ack_retry();
1177: 
1178: 	for (phy_idx = 0; phy_idx < PHY_CHNL_NUM; phy_idx++)
1179: 	{
1180: 		mb_phy_chnl_cb_t *phy = &phy_chnl_x_cb[phy_idx];
1181: 		mb_log_chnl_cb_t *logs;
1182: 		mb_chnl_ack_t failure;
1183: 		u8 log_idx;
1184: 
1185: 		u32 claim_flags = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
1186: 		if ((phy->tx_state != CHNL_STATE_BUSY) || !phy->busy_since_ms ||
1187: 			((u32)(rtos_get_time() - phy->busy_since_ms) < MB_PHY_CHNL_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS))
1188: 		{
1189: 			mb_chnl_exit_critical(claim_flags);
1190: 			continue;
1191: 		}
1192: 		phy->tx_state = CHNL_STATE_IDLE;
1193: 		phy->busy_since_ms = 0;
1194: 		mb_chnl_exit_critical(claim_flags);
1195: 
1196: 		logs = (mb_log_chnl_cb_t *)phy_chnl_log_chnl_list[phy_idx];
1197: 		log_idx = GET_LOG_CHNL_ID(phy->tx_log_chnl);
1198: 		if (log_idx >= phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_idx])
1199: 			continue;
1200: 
1201: 		phy->tx_fault_cnt++;
1202: 		phy->tx_fault_cnt |= 0x20000000;
1203: 		bk_mailbox_tx_timeout((mailbox_endpoint_t)phy_idx);
1204: 		phy->recovering = 1;
1205: 		memset(&failure, 0, sizeof(failure));
1206: 		failure.hdr.cmd = phy->tx_hdr_cmd;
1207: 		failure.hdr.state = CHNL_STATE_COM_FAIL;
1208: 		if (logs[log_idx].tx_cmpl_isr)
1209: 			logs[log_idx].tx_cmpl_isr(logs[log_idx].isr_param, &failure);
1210: 		mb_chnl_fail_pending(logs, phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_idx]);
1211: 		mb_chnl_notify(logs, phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_idx],
1212: 				   MB_CHNL_EVENT_TX_TIMEOUT);
1213: 		if (mb_phy_chnl_send_reset(phy_idx, phy->tx_log_chnl) == BK_OK)
1214: 			mb_chnl_notify(logs, phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_idx],
1215: 					   MB_CHNL_EVENT_ABORT_SENT);
1216: 		else
1217: 			mb_chnl_notify(logs, phy_chnl_log_chnl_num[phy_idx],
1218: 					   MB_CHNL_EVENT_ABORT_FAILED);
1219: 	}
1220: 
1221: 	poll_flags = mb_chnl_enter_critical();
1222: 	s_poll_active = 0;
1223: 	mb_chnl_exit_critical(poll_flags);
1224: }

153: 		rtos_delay_milliseconds(AP_BRIDGE_LOG_RETRY_MS);
154: 	}
155: 	s_ap_bridge.stats.rx_queue_fail++;

158: static u16 ap_bridge_tx_count(void)
159: {
160: 	if (s_ap_bridge.tx_rd <= s_ap_bridge.tx_wr)
161: 		return s_ap_bridge.tx_wr - s_ap_bridge.tx_rd;
162: 	return sizeof(s_ap_bridge.tx_ring) - (s_ap_bridge.tx_rd - s_ap_bridge.tx_wr);
163: }

165: static void ap_bridge_drain_tx(void)
166: {
167: 	u8 data[MB_CHNL_BUFF_LEN];
168: 	u16 count;
169: 	u16 length;
170: 	u16 written;
171: 	u16 i;
172: 
173: 	while (s_ap_bridge.link_ready)
174: 	{
175: 		rtos_lock_mutex(&s_ap_bridge.tx_mutex);
176: 		count = ap_bridge_tx_count();
177: 		if (!count)
178: 		{
179: 			rtos_unlock_mutex(&s_ap_bridge.tx_mutex);
180: 			break;
181: 		}
182: 		length = MIN(count, (u16)sizeof(data));
183: 		length = MIN(length, bk_mb_uart_write_ready(MB_UART0));
184: 		if (!length)
185: 		{
186: 			rtos_unlock_mutex(&s_ap_bridge.tx_mutex);
187: 			break;
188: 		}
189: 
190: 		for (i = 0; i < length; i++)
191: 			data[i] = s_ap_bridge.tx_ring[(s_ap_bridge.tx_rd + i) %
192: 							 sizeof(s_ap_bridge.tx_ring)];
193: 
194: 		written = bk_mb_uart_write(MB_UART0, data, length);
195: 		if (!written)
196: 		{
197: 			rtos_unlock_mutex(&s_ap_bridge.tx_mutex);
198: 			break;
199: 		}
200: 		if (written < length)
201: 			s_ap_bridge.stats.tx_partial++;
202: 
203: 		s_ap_bridge.tx_rd = (s_ap_bridge.tx_rd + written) %
204: 					 sizeof(s_ap_bridge.tx_ring);
205: 		s_ap_bridge.stats.tx_bytes += written;
206: 		rtos_unlock_mutex(&s_ap_bridge.tx_mutex);
207: 	}
208: }

210: static void ap_bridge_task(beken_thread_arg_t arg)
211: {
212: 	u8 input[MB_CHNL_BUFF_LEN];
213: 	u8 line[AP_BRIDGE_LOG_LINE_SIZE];
214: 	u16 line_length = 0;
215: 	u8 active_mode = AP_CONSOLE_OUTPUT_LOG;
216: 	bool line_continues = false;
217: 
218: 	(void)arg;
219: 	for (;;)
220: 	{
221: 		u32 events;
222: 		u32 flags;
223: 		u16 input_length;
224: 		u16 index;
225: 		u8 ready_set;
226: 		u8 ready_clear;
227: 		u8 ready_before;
228: 		bk_err_t ret = rtos_get_semaphore(&s_ap_bridge.sem,
229: 			line_length ? AP_BRIDGE_LOG_FLUSH_MS : 20);
230: 
231: 		bk_mb_uart_poll(MB_UART0);
232: 
233: 		flags = rtos_disable_int();
234: 		events = s_ap_bridge.events;
235: 		s_ap_bridge.events = 0;
236: 		ready_set = s_ap_bridge.ready_set;
237: 		ready_clear = s_ap_bridge.ready_clear;
238: 		ready_before = s_ap_bridge.ready_flags;
239: 		s_ap_bridge.ready_set = 0;
240: 		s_ap_bridge.ready_clear = 0;
241: 		rtos_enable_int(flags);
242: 
243: 		if (events & (AP_BRIDGE_EVENT_DOWN | AP_BRIDGE_EVENT_RESET |
244: 			      AP_BRIDGE_EVENT_TIMEOUT))
245: 		{
246: 			ready_clear |= AP_BRIDGE_READY_MBUART;
247: 		}
248: 		s_ap_bridge.ready_flags |= ready_set;
249: 		s_ap_bridge.ready_flags &= ~ready_clear;
250: 		/* poll() may complete recovery in the same iteration that consumes an
251: 		 * older timeout/reset event.  The driver's current state is the final
252: 		 * authority for the MBUART gate, so a stale event cannot clear a newer
253: 		 * READY notification permanently.
254: 		 */
255: 		if (bk_mb_uart_is_link_ready(MB_UART0))
256: 			s_ap_bridge.ready_flags |= AP_BRIDGE_READY_MBUART;
257: 		else
258: 			s_ap_bridge.ready_flags &= ~AP_BRIDGE_READY_MBUART;
259: 		s_ap_bridge.link_ready =
260: 			(s_ap_bridge.ready_flags & AP_BRIDGE_READY_ALL) ==
261: 			AP_BRIDGE_READY_ALL && bk_mb_uart_is_link_ready(MB_UART0);
262: 
263: 		if (s_ap_bridge.mode_applied_generation !=
264: 			s_ap_bridge.mode_generation)
265: 		{
266: 			if (line_length)
267: 				ap_bridge_log_output(line, line_length, !line_continues);
268: 			line_length = 0;
269: 			line_continues = false;
270: 			active_mode = s_ap_bridge.requested_mode;
271: 			s_ap_bridge.output_mode = active_mode;
272: 			s_ap_bridge.mode_applied_generation =
273: 				s_ap_bridge.mode_generation;
274: 			rtos_set_semaphore(&s_ap_bridge.mode_sem);
275: 		}
276: 
277: 		do
278: 		{
279: 			input_length = bk_mb_uart_read(MB_UART0, input, sizeof(input));
280: 			s_ap_bridge.stats.rx_bytes += input_length;
281: 			if (active_mode == AP_CONSOLE_OUTPUT_RAW)
282: 			{
283: 				if (input_length && !shell_log_raw_data_nonblock(input, input_length))
284: 					s_ap_bridge.stats.rx_queue_fail++;
285: 				continue;
286: 			}
287: 
288: 			for (index = 0; index < input_length; index++)
289: 			{
290: 				line[line_length++] = input[index];
291: 				if (input[index] == '\n' || line_length == sizeof(line))
292: 				{
293: 					bool complete = input[index] == '\n';
294: 
295: 					ap_bridge_log_output(line, line_length,
296: 							     !line_continues);
297: 					line_length = 0;
298: 					line_continues = !complete;
299: 				}
300: 			}
301: 		} while (input_length != 0);
302: 
303: 		if (ret == kTimeoutErr && line_length &&
304: 			active_mode == AP_CONSOLE_OUTPUT_LOG)
305: 		{
306: 			ap_bridge_log_output(line, line_length, !line_continues);
307: 			line_length = 0;
308: 			line_continues = true;
309: 		}
310: 
311: 		ap_bridge_drain_tx();
312: 
313: 		if (events & (AP_BRIDGE_EVENT_DOWN | AP_BRIDGE_EVENT_RESET |
314: 			      AP_BRIDGE_EVENT_TIMEOUT))
315: 		{
316: 			u32 now = rtos_get_time();
317: 
318: 			s_ap_bridge.stats.link_down++;
319: 			if (events & AP_BRIDGE_EVENT_RESET)
320: 				s_ap_bridge.stats.reset++;
321: 			if (events & AP_BRIDGE_EVENT_TIMEOUT)
322: 				s_ap_bridge.stats.timeout++;
323: 			if ((ready_before & (AP_BRIDGE_READY_IPC |
324: 					     AP_BRIDGE_READY_PWC)) ==
325: 				(AP_BRIDGE_READY_IPC | AP_BRIDGE_READY_PWC) &&
326: 				(u32)(now - s_ap_bridge.last_down_log_ms) >= 1000)
327: 			{
328: 				s_ap_bridge.last_down_log_ms = now;
329: 				BK_LOGW(AP_BRIDGE_TAG,
330: 					"link down event=%x queued=%u ready=%x\r\n",
331: 					events, ap_bridge_tx_count(),
332: 					s_ap_bridge.ready_flags);
333: 			}
334: 			if (!s_ap_bridge.link_ready)
335: 				shell_ap_console_link_down();
336: 		}
337: 	}
338: }

340: bk_err_t ap_console_bridge_init(void)
341: {
342: 	bk_err_t ret;
343: 
344: 	memset(&s_ap_bridge, 0, sizeof(s_ap_bridge));
345: 	ret = bk_pm_module_vote_sleep_ctrl(PM_SLEEP_MODULE_NAME_MAILBOX, 0, 0);
346: 	if (ret != BK_OK)
347: 		return ret;
348: 	ret = rtos_init_mutex(&s_ap_bridge.tx_mutex);
349: 	if (ret != BK_OK)
350: 		goto init_fail_vote;
351: 	ret = rtos_init_semaphore(&s_ap_bridge.sem, 1);
352: 	if (ret != BK_OK)
353: 		goto init_fail_mutex;
354: 	ret = rtos_init_semaphore(&s_ap_bridge.mode_sem, 1);
355: 	if (ret != BK_OK)
356: 		goto init_fail_sem;
357: 
358: 	ret = rtos_create_thread(&s_ap_bridge.thread,
359: 					 BEKEN_DEFAULT_WORKER_PRIORITY,
360: 					 "ap_console", ap_bridge_task, 3072, NULL);
361: 	if (ret != BK_OK)
362: 	{
363: 		rtos_deinit_semaphore(&s_ap_bridge.mode_sem);
364: 		rtos_deinit_semaphore(&s_ap_bridge.sem);
365: 		goto init_fail_mutex;
366: 	}
367: 
368: 	ret = bk_mb_uart_dev_init(MB_UART0);
369: 	if (ret != BK_OK)
370: 	{
371: 		rtos_delete_thread(&s_ap_bridge.thread);
372: 		rtos_deinit_semaphore(&s_ap_bridge.mode_sem);
373: 		rtos_deinit_semaphore(&s_ap_bridge.sem);
374: 		goto init_fail_mutex;
375: 	}
376: 
377: 	ret = bk_mb_uart_register_rx_isr(MB_UART0, ap_bridge_mb_rx, NULL);
378: 	if (ret == BK_OK)
379: 		ret = bk_mb_uart_register_tx_isr(MB_UART0, ap_bridge_mb_tx, NULL);
380: 	if (ret == BK_OK)
381: 		ret = bk_mb_uart_register_event_callback(MB_UART0, ap_bridge_mb_event, NULL);
382: 	if (ret != BK_OK)
383: 	{
384: 		bk_mb_uart_dev_deinit(MB_UART0);
385: 		rtos_delete_thread(&s_ap_bridge.thread);
386: 		rtos_deinit_semaphore(&s_ap_bridge.mode_sem);
387: 		rtos_deinit_semaphore(&s_ap_bridge.sem);
388: 		goto init_fail_mutex;
389: 	}
390: 
391: 	ap_bridge_wake(AP_BRIDGE_EVENT_RX | AP_BRIDGE_EVENT_TX);
392: 	BK_LOGI(AP_BRIDGE_TAG, "init owner=MB_UART0 tx_ring=%u mode=LOG\r\n",
393: 		(unsigned)sizeof(s_ap_bridge.tx_ring));
394: 	return BK_OK;
395: 
396: init_fail_sem:
397: 	rtos_deinit_semaphore(&s_ap_bridge.sem);
398: init_fail_mutex:
399: 	rtos_deinit_mutex(&s_ap_bridge.tx_mutex);
400: init_fail_vote:
401: 	bk_pm_module_vote_sleep_ctrl(PM_SLEEP_MODULE_NAME_MAILBOX, 1, 0);
402: 	return ret;
403: }

405: u16 ap_console_bridge_write(const u8 *data, u16 length)
406: {
407: 	u16 written = 0;
408: 
409: 	if (!data || !length || !s_ap_bridge.link_ready)
410: 		return 0;
411: 
412: 	rtos_lock_mutex(&s_ap_bridge.tx_mutex);
413: 	while (written < length)
414: 	{
415: 		u16 next = (s_ap_bridge.tx_wr + 1) % sizeof(s_ap_bridge.tx_ring);
416: 		if (next == s_ap_bridge.tx_rd)
417: 			break;
418: 		s_ap_bridge.tx_ring[s_ap_bridge.tx_wr] = data[written++];
419: 		s_ap_bridge.tx_wr = next;
420: 	}
421: 	rtos_unlock_mutex(&s_ap_bridge.tx_mutex);
422: 	if (written < length)
423: 	{
424: 		s_ap_bridge.stats.tx_drop += length - written;
425: 	}
426: 	if (written)
427: 		ap_bridge_wake(AP_BRIDGE_EVENT_TX);
428: 	return written;
429: }

431: void ap_console_bridge_purge_tx(void)

435: 	s_ap_bridge.tx_rd = s_ap_bridge.tx_wr;
436: 	rtos_unlock_mutex(&s_ap_bridge.tx_mutex);

151: static void mb_uart_tx_complete(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *ack,
152:                                 int result, void *arg)
153: {
154:   uint8_t command;
155:   bool failed;
156: 
157:   (void)arg;
158:   /* The mailbox transport invokes completion callbacks with interrupts
159:    * disabled, so this callback updates UART state directly.
160:    */
161:   command = ack == NULL ? g_uart.transaction_command :
162:             bk7258_mb_header_cmd(ack);
163:   failed = result < 0 || !valid_ack(ack) ||
164:            (ack != NULL && (ack->payload_address & 2u) != 0);
165: 
166:   if (ack != NULL && valid_ack(ack))
167:     {
168:       g_uart.peer_rts = (ack->payload_address & 1u) != 0;
169:       g_uart.peer_rts_known = true;
170:     }
171: 
172:   if (result == -ETIMEDOUT || result == -ECONNRESET)
173:     {
174:       g_uart.peer_rts_known = false;
175:       g_uart.state_pending = true;
176:     }
177: 
178:   if (command == BK7258_MB_UART_DATA && g_uart.tx_inflight != 0)
179:     {
180:       if (!failed)
181:         {
182:           g_uart.tx_read = (g_uart.tx_read + g_uart.tx_inflight) %
183:                            MB_UART_TX_SIZE;
184:           g_uart.tx_retry_count = 0;
185:         }
186:       else if (result == -ETIMEDOUT || result == -ECONNRESET)
187:         {
188:           /* A failed/unknown ACK cannot tell whether CP consumed the bytes.
189:            * Drop this local chunk rather than replaying terminal characters.
190:            */
191: 
192:           g_uart.tx_read = (g_uart.tx_read + g_uart.tx_inflight) %
193:                            MB_UART_TX_SIZE;
194:           g_uart.stats.tx_unknown++;
195:           g_uart.tx_retry_count = 0;
196:           g_uart.stats.resets++;
197:         }
198:       else
199:         {
200:           g_uart.stats.remote_fail++;
201:           g_uart.state_pending = true;
202:           if (g_uart.tx_retry_count == 0)
203:             {
204:               /* Keep tx_read unchanged.  The same chunk may be copied again
205:                * once STATE recovery succeeds, but only once.
206:                */
207: 
208:               g_uart.tx_retry_count = 1;
209:               g_uart.stats.tx_retry++;
210:             }
211:           else
212:             {
213:               g_uart.tx_read = (g_uart.tx_read + g_uart.tx_inflight) %
214:                                MB_UART_TX_SIZE;
215:               g_uart.tx_retry_count = 0;
216:               g_uart.stats.tx_retry_drop++;
217:             }
218:         }
219: 
220:       g_uart.tx_inflight = 0;
221:     }
222:   else if (command == BK7258_MB_UART_STATE && failed)
223:     {
224:       g_uart.stats.remote_fail++;
225:       /* The transport invokes this completion before it changes READY to
226:        * ABORTING.  Always retain a STATE request so RESET recovery has a
227:        * probe to send after it reaches PROBING.
228:        */
229: 
230:       g_uart.state_pending = true;
231:     }
232: 
233:   g_uart.transaction_busy = false;
234:   nxsem_post(&g_uart.worker_sem);
235: }

237: static int mb_uart_receive(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message,
238:                            uint8_t *ack_flags, void *arg)
239: {
240:   uint8_t command = bk7258_mb_header_cmd(message);
241:   uint16_t length = message->payload_length;
242:   uint16_t first;
243:   bool failed = false;
244:   bool malformed = false;
245: 
246:   (void)arg;
247:   if (ack_flags == NULL)
248:     {
249:       return -EINVAL;
250:     }
251: 
252:   if (command != BK7258_MB_UART_DATA && command != BK7258_MB_UART_STATE)
253:     {
254:       g_uart.stats.bad_flags++;
255:       failed = true;
256:       malformed = true;
257:     }
258:   else if ((message->flags & ~1u) != 0)
259:     {
260:       g_uart.stats.bad_flags++;
261:       failed = true;
262:       malformed = true;
263:     }
264:   else if (message->crc8 != 0)
265:     {
266:       g_uart.stats.bad_crc++;
267:       g_uart.sticky_status |= MB_UART_STATUS_PARITY;
268:       failed = true;
269:       malformed = true;
270:     }
271:   else if (message->reserved != 0)
272:     {
273:       g_uart.stats.bad_reserved++;
274:       failed = true;
275:       malformed = true;
276:     }
277: 
278:   if (!failed && command == BK7258_MB_UART_DATA)
279:     {
280:       if (message->payload_address != BK7258_MB_UART_RX_ADDRESS)
281:         {
282:           g_uart.stats.bad_pointer++;
283:           failed = true;
284:           malformed = true;
285:         }
286:       else if (length == 0 || length > BK7258_MB_UART_CHUNK_SIZE)
287:         {
288:           g_uart.stats.bad_length++;
289:           failed = true;
290:           malformed = true;
291:         }
292:       else if (!bk7258_mailbox_link_ready())
293:         {
294:           failed = true;
295:         }
296:       else if (rx_free() < length)
297:         {
298:           g_uart.stats.rx_overflow++;
299:           g_uart.sticky_status |= MB_UART_STATUS_OVF;
300:           failed = true;
301:         }
302:       else
303:         {
304:           const uint8_t *source =
305:             (const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)BK7258_MB_UART_RX_ADDRESS;
306: 
307:           __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
308:           first = MB_UART_RX_SIZE - g_uart.rx_write;
309:           if (first > length)
310:             {
311:               first = length;
312:             }
313: 
314:           memcpy(&g_uart.rx_ring[g_uart.rx_write], source, first);
315:           if (first != length)
316:             {
317:               memcpy(g_uart.rx_ring, source + first, length - first);
318:             }
319: 
320:           g_uart.rx_write = (g_uart.rx_write + length) % MB_UART_RX_SIZE;
321:           g_uart.stats.data_rx++;
322:           g_uart.stats.rx_bytes += length;
323:         }
324:     }
325:   else if (!failed)
326:     {
327:       if (message->payload_address != 0 || message->payload_length != 0)
328:         {
329:           g_uart.stats.bad_length++;
330:           failed = true;
331:           malformed = true;
332:         }
333:       else
334:         {
335:           g_uart.stats.state_rx++;
336:         }
337:     }
338: 
339:   if (!malformed)
340:     {
341:       bool old_peer_rts = g_uart.peer_rts;
342: 
343:       g_uart.peer_rts = (message->flags & 1u) != 0;
344:       g_uart.peer_rts_known = true;
345:       if (old_peer_rts && !g_uart.peer_rts)
346:         {
347:           nxsem_post(&g_uart.worker_sem);
348:         }
349:     }
350: 
351:   update_local_rts();
352:   *ack_flags = (g_uart.local_rts ? 1u : 0u) | (failed ? 2u : 0u);
353:   nxsem_post(&g_uart.worker_sem);
354:   return malformed ? -EPROTO : OK;
355: }

379: static int send_data_locked(void)
380: {
381:   struct bk7258_mb_wire_message message;
382:   uint8_t *destination =
383:     (uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)BK7258_MB_UART_TX_ADDRESS;
384:   uint16_t length = tx_count();
385:   uint16_t first;
386:   int ret;
387: 
388:   if (length > BK7258_MB_UART_CHUNK_SIZE)
389:     {
390:       length = BK7258_MB_UART_CHUNK_SIZE;
391:     }
392: 
393:   if (length == 0 || g_uart.peer_rts)
394:     {
395:       return -EAGAIN;
396:     }
397: 
398:   first = MB_UART_TX_SIZE - g_uart.tx_read;
399:   if (first > length)
400:     {
401:       first = length;
402:     }
403: 
404:   memcpy(destination, &g_uart.tx_ring[g_uart.tx_read], first);
405:   if (first != length)
406:     {
407:       memcpy(destination + first, g_uart.tx_ring, length - first);
408:     }
409: 
410:   memset(&message, 0, sizeof(message));
411:   message.header = bk7258_mb_make_header(BK7258_MB_UART_DATA, 0, 0, 0,
412:                                          BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX);
413:   message.payload_address = BK7258_MB_UART_TX_ADDRESS;
414:   message.payload_length = length;
415:   message.flags = g_uart.local_rts ? 1u : 0u;
416:   __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
417:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_send_wire(BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX, &message,
418:                                   mb_uart_tx_complete, NULL);
419:   if (ret == OK)
420:     {
421:       g_uart.transaction_busy = true;
422:       g_uart.transaction_command = BK7258_MB_UART_DATA;
423:       g_uart.tx_inflight = length;
424:       g_uart.stats.data_tx++;
425:     }
426: 
427:   return ret;

430: static int mb_uart_worker(int argc, char **argv)
431: {
432:   (void)argc;
433:   (void)argv;
434: 
435:   for (;;)
436:     {
437:       bk7258_mb_uart_callback_t callback;
438:       void *callback_arg;
439:       irqstate_t flags;
440:       enum bk7258_mb_link_state link;
441: 
442:       (void)nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible(&g_uart.worker_sem,
443:                                            MB_UART_WORK_INTERVAL);
444:       nxsem_reset(&g_uart.worker_sem, 0);
445:       link = bk7258_mailbox_link_state();
446:       flags = up_irq_save();
447: 
448:       if (!g_uart.transaction_busy)
449:         {
450:           if (link == BK7258_MB_LINK_PROBING && g_uart.state_pending)
451:             {
452:               (void)send_state_locked();
453:             }
454:           else if (link == BK7258_MB_LINK_READY)
455:             {
456:               if (g_uart.state_pending)
457:                 {
458:                   (void)send_state_locked();
459:                 }
460:               else
461:                 {
462:                   (void)send_data_locked();
463:                 }
464:             }
465:         }
466: 
467:       callback = g_uart.callback;
468:       callback_arg = g_uart.callback_arg;
469:       up_irq_restore(flags);
470: 
471:       if (callback != NULL)
472:         {
473:           callback(callback_arg);
474:         }
475:     }
476: 
477:   return OK;
478: }

561: ssize_t bk7258_mbox_uart_write(const uint8_t *data, size_t length)
562: {
563:   irqstate_t flags;
564:   uint16_t available;
565:   uint16_t written;
566:   uint16_t first;
567: 
568:   if (data == NULL && length != 0)
569:     {
570:       return -EINVAL;
571:     }
572: 
573:   if (length == 0)
574:     {
575:       return 0;
576:     }
577: 
578:   flags = up_irq_save();
579:   available = tx_free();
580:   written = length > available ? available : length;
581:   first = MB_UART_TX_SIZE - g_uart.tx_write;
582:   if (first > written)
583:     {
584:       first = written;
585:     }
586: 
587:   memcpy(&g_uart.tx_ring[g_uart.tx_write], data, first);
588:   if (first != written)
589:     {
590:       memcpy(g_uart.tx_ring, data + first, written - first);
591:     }
592: 
593:   g_uart.tx_write = (g_uart.tx_write + written) % MB_UART_TX_SIZE;
594:   g_uart.stats.write_calls++;
595:   g_uart.stats.write_bytes += written;
596:   if (written < length)
597:     {
598:       g_uart.stats.short_writes++;

601:   up_irq_restore(flags);
602:   if (g_uart.initialized && written != 0)
603:     {

605:     }
606: 
607:   return written;

610: ssize_t bk7258_mbox_uart_read(uint8_t *data, size_t length,

612: {
613:   irqstate_t flags;
614:   uint16_t available;
615:   uint16_t count;
616:   uint16_t first;
617: 
618:   if (data == NULL || length == 0)
619:     {

621:     }
622: 
623:   flags = up_irq_save();
624:   available = rx_count();
625:   count = length > available ? available : length;
626:   first = MB_UART_RX_SIZE - g_uart.rx_read;
627:   if (first > count)
628:     {
629:       first = count;
630:     }
631: 
632:   memcpy(data, &g_uart.rx_ring[g_uart.rx_read], first);
633:   if (first != count)
634:     {
635:       memcpy(data + first, g_uart.rx_ring, count - first);
636:     }

638:   g_uart.rx_read = (g_uart.rx_read + count) % MB_UART_RX_SIZE;

643:     }

654:       nxsem_post(&g_uart.worker_sem);
655:     }
656: 
657:   return count;
658: }

struct timespec after;

usleep(10000);
clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &after);
```

```c

```

- GPIO12, GPIO9, GPIO52, and `/dev/pwm0` are involved in the power-key vibration service.

1. PSRAM online/info plus allocator-owned pattern test.
2. `board_buttons()` snapshot and `/dev/gpio0..2` read/pintype checks.
3. Procfs read checks.
4. Mailbox link-state check.
5. Bounded `/dev/ttyMB0` write followed by bounded transport drain, if CP-side output is acceptable.
6. Heartbeat indirect liveness check through link state, reset generation, and procfs task visibility.
7. `wlan0` interface presence/status.
8. `/dev/pwm0` open/close only.
9. Monotonic clock progression.
10. Optional `/dev/null` and `/dev/zero` checks.

Manual or explicitly opt-in tests:

- Green/red LED visual indication.
- LCD/QSPI initialization or panel command test.

Do not invoke automatically:

- Raw PSRAM address scans.
- `bk7258_psram_shutdown()`.
- Mailbox reset or raw wire transactions.
- UART reads that consume NSH input.
- PWM configuration/start/stop.
- LCD reset/init/QSPI remux.
- Camera or vibration operations.

The current builtin stack is 2048 bytes. A self-test using formatted output, procfs buffers, PSRAM metadata, and multiple device checks should use a larger stack, such as 4096 bytes, when the application metadata is eventually updated.

189:       ret = g_callback == NULL ? -ENOSYS : g_callback(&desc->message);
190:       g_processing_order = 0;
191:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
192:         {
193:           g_stats.descriptor_deferred++;
194:           break;
195:         }
196: 
197:       desc->used = false;
198:     }
199: 
200:   while ((desc = mbox_oldest_desc(false)) != NULL)
201:     {
202:       g_processing_order = desc->order;
203:       ret = g_callback == NULL ? -ENOSYS : g_callback(&desc->message);
204:       g_processing_order = 0;
205:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)

208:         }

255:       memcpy(&desc->message, (const void *)(uintptr_t)address,
256:              sizeof(desc->message));
257:       desc->order = ++g_rx_order;
258:       desc->used = true;
259:       g_stats.rx_messages++;

263:   mbox_process_desc();

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_qspi.c
3:  *
4:  * BK7258 QSPI1 command-channel driver (no DMA, cmd_c/cmd_d indirect command
5:  * path only).  Register layout source: bk_avdk_smp release/v3.1.1
6:  * ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/qspi_struct.h and hal/qspi_ll.h.  QSPI0
7:  * and QSPI1 are two identical controller instances differing only in base
8:  * address and which fixed GPIO group is wired to their CLK/CSN/IO0-3
9:  * signal lines.
10:  *
11:  * Corrected from QSPI0 to QSPI1 (2026-07-31): this driver originally
12:  * targeted QSPI0 (base 0x46040000, GPIO22/23/24/25) because that is the
13:  * pin group used by bk_avdk_smp's generic
14:  * projects/spi_lcd_example/qspi_lcd_example reference configs. Those
15:  * reference projects' own hardware wires their LCD to that pin group, but
16:  * this board's actual schematic
17:  * (AIDK_AI玩具开发板_原理图.pdf sheet 2/6 main chip pin table + sheet 5/6
18:  * CN5 single-screen connector) shows the panel's LCD_QSPI_CLK/CS/D0/D1 net
19:  * labels are wired to chip pins 35/34/33/32 = P2/P3/P4/P5 =
20:  * GPIO2/GPIO3/GPIO4/GPIO5, which per the chip's pinmux table
21:  * (bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/gpio_map.h GPIO_DEV_MAP)
22:  * carry QSPI1_CLK/QSPI1_CSN/QSPI1_IO0/QSPI1_IO1 (function-select index 6),
23:  * not QSPI0.  Symptom that led to this fix: with the QSPI0 assumption,
24:  * bk7258_qspi0_send_cmd() always timed out on the very first init command
25:  * (0xFE) -- GPIO22-25 were pinmuxed to QSPI0, but the panel is not
26:  * physically wired to those pins, so cmd_start_done never asserts and the
27:  * 10000-iteration wait always exhausts.  See
28:  * hardware/bk7258_memorymap.h's BK7258_QSPI1_BASE comment for the full
29:  * schematic evidence chain (chip pin numbers, net names, gpio_map.h
30:  * excerpt).
31:  *
32:  * Note the schematic's literal net names ("LCD_QSPI_D0" etc.) do NOT
33:  * match the SoC's real hardware role for these pins (CLK/CSN, not data
34:  * lines) -- PCB net labels are the board designer's arbitrary
35:  * connector-pin numbering convention, not a statement about which SoC
36:  * peripheral function is actually multiplexed onto that pad.  The real
37:  * role is only knowable from gpio_map.h's per-pin function array, which is
38:  * what this driver's pin/function assignments below are built from.
39:  *
40:  * Register offsets (byte offset from BK7258_QSPI1_BASE, word index in
41:  * qspi_hw_t from qspi_struct.h in parentheses) -- identical layout to
42:  * QSPI0, only the base address differs:
43:  *   glb_ctrl    0x08 (REG_0x02) - bit[0] soft_reset, bit[1] bps_clkgate
44:  *   cmd_c_l     0x40 (REG_0x10)
45:  *   cmd_c_h     0x44 (REG_0x11)
46:  *   cmd_c_cfg1  0x48 (REG_0x12)
47:  *   cmd_c_cfg2  0x4c (REG_0x13) - bit[0] cmd_start
48:  *   cmd_d_l     0x50 (REG_0x14)
49:  *   cmd_d_h     0x54 (REG_0x15)
50:  *   cmd_d_cfg1  0x58 (REG_0x16)
51:  *   cmd_d_cfg2  0x5c (REG_0x17) - bit[0] cmd_start
52:  *   status      0x70 (REG_0x1c) - bit[2] cmd_start_done
53:  *   status_clr  0x6c (REG_0x1b) - bit[2] clr_cmd_start_done
54:  *
55:  * The "command done" flag is carried by the status register's
56:  * cmd_start_done bit, not by core_status (REG_0x03, byte offset 0x0c),
57:  * which is an unused, un-bitfielded raw word in the vendor headers and is
58:  * never read by qspi_ll_is_cmd_start_done()/qspi_ll_wait_cmd_done().  The
59:  * start trigger is not a separate register either: it is the cmd_start bit
60:  * inside each channel's own cfg2 register (cmd_c_cfg2 for the send path,
61:  * cmd_d_cfg2 for the read path), matching qspi_ll_cmd_c_start() and
62:  * qspi_ll_cmd_d_start().
63:  *
64:  * Pinmux: the QSPI1 controller's four signal lines (CLK/CSN/IO0/IO1) are
65:  * shared, multiplexed GPIO pads (GPIO_2/3/4/5 on this SoC), not dedicated
66:  * pins.  Each pad defaults to plain GPIO after reset and must be switched
67:  * to QSPI1 mode via the "second function" pinmux mechanism before the
68:  * controller's TX/RX lines are actually connected to the pad -- without
69:  * this step cmd_start_done never asserts because the panel never receives
70:  * the command.  Source of the function-select index (6) for QSPI1 on
71:  * GPIO_2/3/4/5: bk_avdk_smp release/v3.1.1
72:  * ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/gpio_map.h gpio_map_table (QSPI1_CLK/
73:  * CSN/IO0/IO1 are the 7th entry, index 6, in each pin's per-function
74:  * array).  The pinmux register plumbing itself (BK7258_GPIO_SYS_BASE etc.)
75:  * is shared with bk7258_gpio.c; see bk7258_gpio_set_function().
76:  *
77:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
78:  ****************************************************************************/
79:

103: #define QSPI_CMD_C_H               QSPI_REG(0x44u)
104: #define QSPI_CMD_C_CFG1            QSPI_REG(0x48u)
105: #define QSPI_CMD_C_CFG2            QSPI_REG(0x4cu)
106: 
107: #define QSPI_CMD_D_L               QSPI_REG(0x50u)
108: #define QSPI_CMD_D_H               QSPI_REG(0x54u)
109: #define QSPI_CMD_D_CFG1            QSPI_REG(0x58u)
110: #define QSPI_CMD_D_CFG2            QSPI_REG(0x5cu)
111: 
112: #define QSPI_STATUS                QSPI_REG(0x70u)
113: #define QSPI_STATUS_CMD_START_DONE (1u << 2)
114: 
115: #define QSPI_STATUS_CLR                 QSPI_REG(0x6cu)
116: #define QSPI_STATUS_CLR_CMD_START_DONE  (1u << 2)
117: 
118: #define QSPI_CMD_START_BIT         (1u << 0)
119: 
120: /* Matches qspi_ll_wait_cmd_done()'s 10000-iteration bound
121:  * (ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/qspi_ll.h) instead of looping forever,
122:  * so a pinmux or wiring problem produces a diagnosable timeout rather than
123:  * an unrecoverable hang. */
124: #define QSPI_WAIT_DONE_MAX_ITER    10000
125: 
126: static bool bk7258_qspi0_wait_done(void)
127: {
128:   int i;
129: 
130:   for (i = 0; i < QSPI_WAIT_DONE_MAX_ITER; i++)
131:     {
132:       if ((getreg32(QSPI_STATUS) & QSPI_STATUS_CMD_START_DONE) != 0)
133:         {
134:           break;
135:         }
136: 
137:       up_udelay(1);
138:     }
139: 
140:   /* Clear cmd_start_done (write 1 then 0), matching qspi_ll_wait_cmd_done()
141:    * -- required so a stale "done" flag from this command does not make
142:    * the next command's wait loop return immediately without having
143:    * actually completed. */
144:   modifyreg32(QSPI_STATUS_CLR, 0, QSPI_STATUS_CLR_CMD_START_DONE);
145:   modifyreg32(QSPI_STATUS_CLR, QSPI_STATUS_CLR_CMD_START_DONE, 0);
146: 
147:   return i < QSPI_WAIT_DONE_MAX_ITER;
148: }
149: 
150: void bk7258_qspi0_init(void)
151: {
152:   /* Enable the QSPI1 *module* clock gate first, matching
153:    * qspi_id_init_common()'s documented call order ("1. set clock, 2. set
154:    * gpio as qspi, 3. enable interrupt") in bk_avdk_smp release/v3.1.1
155:    * ap/middleware/driver/qspi/qspi_driver.c.  Without this bit, register
156:    * writes to the QSPI1 block are accepted (no bus fault) but the
157:    * controller's internal command state machine has no clock to run on,
158:    * so cmd_start_done never asserts -- see
159:    * hardware/bk7258_sysctrl.h's BK7258_QSPI1_MODULE_CLK_EN comment for
160:    * the register-map citation and the I2C1 precedent this is modeled
161:    * after. */
162:   modifyreg32(BK7258_SYS_DEVCLK_EN, 0, BK7258_QSPI1_MODULE_CLK_EN);
163: 
164:   /* Switch the 4 shared GPIO pads to QSPI1 mode before touching the
165:    * controller; see file header comment for why this is required and why
166:    * it is QSPI1 (GPIO2-5) rather than QSPI0 (GPIO22-25) on this board. */
167:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(QSPI1_CLK_PIN, QSPI1_PINMUX_FUNCTION);
168:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(QSPI1_CSN_PIN, QSPI1_PINMUX_FUNCTION);
169:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(QSPI1_IO0_PIN, QSPI1_PINMUX_FUNCTION);
170:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(QSPI1_IO1_PIN, QSPI1_PINMUX_FUNCTION);
171: 
172:   putreg32(QSPI_GLB_CTRL_SOFT_RESET, QSPI_GLB_CTRL);
173:   up_udelay(10);
174:   putreg32(0, QSPI_GLB_CTRL);
175: }
176: 
177: bool bk7258_qspi0_send_cmd(uint8_t cmd, const uint8_t *data, uint8_t data_len)
178: {
179:   uint32_t cmd_c_h = (uint32_t)cmd;
180:   uint32_t cmd_c_l = 0;
181:   uint8_t i;
182:

29: {
30:   irqstate_t flags;
31:   uint32_t setbits = value ? BK7258_GPIO_OUTPUT : 0;
32: 
33:   flags = enter_critical_section();
34:   modifyreg32(BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin),
35:               BK7258_GPIO_INPUT_ENABLE | BK7258_GPIO_OUTPUT |
36:               BK7258_GPIO_OUTPUT_DISABLE | BK7258_GPIO_PULL_ENABLE |
37:               BK7258_GPIO_SECOND_FUNCTION,
38:               setbits);
39:   leave_critical_section(flags);
40: }
41: 
42: void bk7258_gpio_write(unsigned int pin, bool value)
43: {
44:   if (value)
45:     {
46:       modifyreg32(BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin), 0, BK7258_GPIO_OUTPUT);
47:     }
48:   else
49:     {
50:       modifyreg32(BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin), BK7258_GPIO_OUTPUT, 0);
51:     }
52: }

55: {
56:   return (getreg32(BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin)) & BK7258_GPIO_INPUT) != 0;

1: #!/bin/bash
2: # autoflash.sh -- flash the BK7258 board without pressing RST by hand.
3: #
4: # How it works
5: # ------------
6: # bk_loader resets the board by pulsing DTR/RTS (CCommPort::do_reset_signal),
7: # but this board has no auto-reset circuit on those lines -- measured: pulsing
8: # either one produces zero bytes.  That is why a human has to press RST while
9: # bk_loader is looping on "Getting Bus...".
10: #
11: # The bootrom only answers the LinkCheck handshake for a short window after a
12: # reset.  Measured on this board: issuing "reboot" over the CP shell gives
13: # about 473 ms of silence (0.005 s -> 0.478 s) before firmware output starts,
14: # and the shell prompt is back at 1.04 s.  So the window is wide enough.
15: #
16: # bk_loader does not take TIOCEXCL on the tty, so a second process can write
17: # into the same port while bk_loader is looping.  Writing "reboot" there makes
18: # the running firmware reset itself -- exactly what pressing RST does, only
19: # scripted.  Verified: "Gotten Bus..." arrives ~0.5 s after the write.
20: #
21: # IMPORTANT: once the bus is taken, anything else written to the port would
22: # corrupt the protocol, so the reboot loop stops the moment "Gotten Bus"
23: # appears in the log.
24: 
25: set -u
26: 
27: ROOT=/home/mi/vela_competition
28: LOADER="$ROOT/bk_loader"
29: DEFAULT_IMAGE="$ROOT/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/package/all-app.bin"
30: RUNTIME_DIR="$ROOT/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/logs/runtime"
31: EXPECTED_SIZE=2646016
32: 
33: PORT=/dev/ttyUSB0
34: PORTNUM=0
35: 
36: # Two independent baud rates, do not conflate them.
37: #
38: # BAUD is only how fast bk_loader talks to the bootrom.  CONSOLE_BAUD is what
39: # the firmware's console runs at, which is fixed by the build (defconfig), so
40: # raising the flash speed must not change it.  Using one variable for both
41: # meant that after "-b 1500000" the post-flash screen opened at 1500000 and
42: # nothing typed into it worked.
43: BAUD=115200
44: CONSOLE_BAUD=115200
45: IMAGE="$DEFAULT_IMAGE"
46: LOG="$RUNTIME_DIR/autoflash.log"
47: REBOOT_TRIES=8
48: REBOOT_INTERVAL=1.5
49: 
50: # Overall timeout is derived from the image size, never hard-coded.
51: #
52: # A fixed 180 s was wrong and actively harmful: 2,646,016 bytes at 115200 baud
53: # is 10 bits per byte on the wire, i.e. ~230 s of writing alone, plus ~10 s of
54: # 64K erase.  timeout(1) killed a real flash at "Writing Flash ... 69%",
55: # leaving the board with an erased-but-incomplete image.  Computed below as
56: # transfer time x 2 plus 60 s of headroom.
57: OVERALL_TIMEOUT=0
58: ATTACH_SERIAL=0
59: SKIP_SIZE_CHECK=0
60: TEST_ONLY=0
61: 
62: usage() {
63:   cat <<'EOF'
64: 用法: autoflash.sh [选项]
65: 
66:   -i <file>    要烧录的镜像，默认 all-app.bin
67:   -p <port>    串口设备，默认 /dev/ttyUSB0
68:   -n <num>     bk_loader 的端口号，默认 0
69:   -b <baud>    烧录波特率，默认 115200（只影响下载速度）
70:   -B <baud>    控制台波特率，默认 115200（固件编译时定死的，一般别改）
71:   -s           跳过 all-app.bin 字节数校验
72:   -a           烧完自动挂上串口看日志
73:   -t           只测握手，不写 flash（用 read 代替 download）
74:   -h           显示本帮助
75: 
76: 说明: 不需要手按 RST。脚本会在 bk_loader 握手循环期间，从另一个进程往
77:       同一个串口写 reboot 来触发软复位。
78: EOF
79: }
80: 
81: while getopts "i:p:n:b:B:sath" opt; do
82:   case "$opt" in
83:     i) IMAGE="$OPTARG" ;;
84:     p) PORT="$OPTARG" ;;
85:     n) PORTNUM="$OPTARG" ;;
86:     b) BAUD="$OPTARG" ;;
87:     B) CONSOLE_BAUD="$OPTARG" ;;
88:     s) SKIP_SIZE_CHECK=1 ;;
89:     a) ATTACH_SERIAL=1 ;;
90:     t) TEST_ONLY=1 ;;
91:     h) usage; exit 0 ;;
92:     *) usage; exit 2 ;;
93:   esac
94: done
95: 
96: die() { echo "错误: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
97: 
98: # ---------------------------------------------------------------- 1. 前置检查
99: 
100: [ -x "$LOADER" ] || die "找不到 bk_loader: $LOADER"
101: [ -f "$IMAGE" ]  || die "找不到镜像: $IMAGE"
102: [ -c "$PORT" ]   || die "串口不存在: $PORT（板子插了吗？）"
103: mkdir -p "$RUNTIME_DIR" || die "无法创建运行记录目录: $RUNTIME_DIR"
104: 
105: SIZE=$(stat -c%s "$IMAGE")
106: SHA=$(sha256sum "$IMAGE" | cut -d' ' -f1)
107: 
108: # 10 bits on the wire per byte (8N1 plus start and stop).
109: XFER_SECS=$(( SIZE * 10 / BAUD ))
110: OVERALL_TIMEOUT=$(( XFER_SECS * 2 + 60 ))
111: 
112: echo "=== 待烧录镜像 ==="
113: echo "  路径   : $IMAGE"
114: echo "  字节数 : $SIZE"
115: echo "  SHA256 : $SHA"

## Conclusion

The immediate timeout is caused by an incomplete BK7258 I2C initialization port, not by the GC2145 address or register table.

`int_status=0x00000410` decodes as:

- bit 10 `START` = 1
- bit 4 `RX_FIFO_EMPTY` = 1
- bit 0 `SM_INT` = 0
- bit 1 `SCL_TIMEOUT` = 0
- bit 3 `ARB_LOST` = 0
- bit 14 `MASTER` = 0
- bit 15 `BUSY` = 0

Thus the START command was accepted into the register, but the I2C state machine never entered master-transmit operation. This is earlier than any GC2145 ACK/NACK decision. A wrong address, unpowered sensor, or missing sensor MCLK would produce a completed address phase followed by a NACK/`SM_INT`, not a permanently latched bare START.

`sm_bus_cfg=0xbc001523` is otherwise correct:

- bit 31 `en` = 1
- bit 30 `inh` = 0
- bits 29/28 idle detection and timeout enabled
- bits 27:26 `clk_src` = 3
- bits 15:6 `freq_div` = 84, the expected 26 MHz → approximately 100 kHz divider
- `scl_cr=4`, `idle_cr=3`

## Primary root cause: missing BK7236v5/BK7258 output-mode configuration

The current driver defines the required extended configuration bits but never writes them:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/hardware/bk7258_i2c1.h:72-74`

  - `BK7258_I2C1_EX_ADDR_H_OUTEN`, bit 1

The current initialization stops after configuring `SM_BUS_CFG`:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_i2c1.c:198-230`

In particular, there is no write to `BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_EX_CFG` at `I2C1_BASE + 0x1c`.

The vendor reference explicitly performs both operations for this silicon family:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/common/hal/i2c_hal.c:60-64`

```c
/* i2c add address/data output mode config in ASIC, since bk7236v5 */
#if (CONFIG_SOC_BK7236XX)
    i2c_ll_enable_addr_output(&hal->hw, hal->id);
    i2c_ll_enable_data_output(&hal->hw, hal->id);
#endif
```

For BK7258, the vendor configuration defines both `CONFIG_SOC_BK7258` and `CONFIG_SOC_BK7236XX`, so that block is compiled. The LL APIs set:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/i2c_ll.h:585-609`
  - `sm_bus_ex_cfg.addr_h_outen = 1`
  - `sm_bus_ex_cfg.data_h_outen = 1`

Equivalent vendor APIs are:

i2c_ll_enable_data_output(...);
```

The expected `SM_BUS_EX_CFG` low bits after initialization are therefore `0x00000003`.

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_i2c1.c:124`

{

              BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_START);
  putreg32(status, BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS);
}

Two concrete initialization defects are present in `bk7258_qspi.c`:

1. **The soft-reset sequence is backwards.**

2. **`QSPI_CONFIG.qspi_en` is never set.**

The omitted **AHBP QSPI1 power-domain vote** can independently produce the same dead-controller symptom if the domain is not already held on by another AP/CP user. Enabling only `SYS_DEVCLK_EN.bit21` is not equivalent to powering the AHBP domain.

Wrong panel power or panel wiring cannot, by itself, explain `cmd_start_done` never setting. QSPI command completion is controller-local; the GC9D01 does not return an acknowledgment for command `0xfe`.

Target code:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_qspi.c:172-175`

Vendor code does the reverse:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/lcd/lcd_spi_driver.c:372-374`

static inline void qspi_ll_enable_soft_reset(qspi_hw_t *hw)
{

{

## Clock details

The current target enables only the QSPI1 leaf gate. It does not program the source selector or source divider used by the vendor.

QSPI1 clock source/divider is in SYSCTRL register word `0x0a`:

```text
Address: 0x44010000 + 0x28 = 0x44010028
bits  6:9  ckdiv_qspi1
bit     10 cksel_qspi1
```

Vendor’s GC9D01 descriptor requests 60 MHz:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_peripheral/src/lcd/spi/lcd_spi_gc9d01.c:73-79`

```c
.clk = LCD_QSPI_60M
```

Vendor’s QSPI-backed SPI initialization chooses:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/lcd/lcd_spi_driver.c:330-334`

```c
src_clk = QSPI_SCLK_480M;
src_clk_div = 7;
```

This gives:

```text
480 MHz / (1 + 7) = 60 MHz
```

The selector values are:

```text
QSPI_CLK_320M = 0
QSPI_CLK_480M = 1
```

Therefore the deterministic 60 MHz SYSCTRL setting is:

```c
#define BK7258_SYS_QSPI1_CLK_CFG   0x44010028u
#define QSPI1_CLK_CFG_MASK         (0x1fu << 6)  /* bits 6..10 */
#define QSPI1_CLK_60M_VALUE        ((7u << 6) | (1u << 10))
                                           /* = 0x5c0 */
```

Then:

```c
modifyreg32(BK7258_SYS_QSPI1_CLK_CFG,
            QSPI1_CLK_CFG_MASK,
            QSPI1_CLK_60M_VALUE);

modifyreg32(0x44010030u, 0, 1u << 21);
```

The QSPI controller’s second-stage divider is `CONFIG.bits8:15`. Vendor’s zero-initialized QSPI configuration leaves this at zero, meaning bypass/divide-by-one for this LCD path.

The vendor GC9D01 is explicitly described as an SPI panel:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_peripheral/src/lcd/spi/lcd_spi_gc9d01.c:81-89`

```c

The vendor SPI path toggles D/C and sends command and data separately:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/lcd/lcd_spi_driver.c:480-506`

```c

/* Payload */

lcd_spi_send_data_with_qspi_indirect_mode(id, data, data_len);

For a one-byte command through QSPI `cmd_c`, vendor uses:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/lcd/lcd_spi_driver.c:390-406`

```c

qspi_hal_set_cmd_c_cfg1(..., 0x3 << (data_len * 2));
qspi_hal_cmd_c_start(...);

The target instead does:

    uint32_t value = 0;

233: bool bk7258_i2c1_write_reg(uint8_t i2c_addr, uint8_t reg, uint8_t value)
234: {
235:   irqstate_t flags;
236:   int ret;
237:   int busy_wait_us;
238: 
239:   /* Wait for the bus to report idle before issuing a new START,
240:    * matching i2c_hardware_memory_write_impl()'s
241:    * i2c_wait_sm_bus_idle() call.  sm_bus_status.busy (bit[15]) lives in
242:    * the same register as INT_STATUS (both are REG_0x05 per
243:    * i2c_struct.h's sm_bus_status union), so BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS is
244:    * read here rather than a separate "status" register.  Without this
245:    * check, if busy is stuck set (e.g. right after
246:    * bk7258_i2c1_init() enables the peripheral while the external bus
247:    * lines are still settling), writing the start bit below would be
248:    * silently ignored by the hardware state machine -- producing
249:    * exactly the "interrupt never fires, write_reg() times out"
250:    * symptom, indistinguishable from a dead/unwired bus without this
251:    * check to rule it out. */
252:   for (busy_wait_us = 0;
253:        (getreg32(BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS) &
254:         BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_BUSY) != 0 && busy_wait_us < 10000;
255:        busy_wait_us += 100)
256:     {
257:       up_udelay(100);
258:     }
259: 
260:   g_i2c1_dev_addr = i2c_addr;
261:   g_i2c1_reg_addr = reg;
262:   g_i2c1_data = value;
263:   g_i2c1_ack_ok = false;
264: 
265:   flags = enter_critical_section();
266: 
267:   /* Write the (7-bit addr << 1 | write-bit=0) byte first, then set
268:    * start=1, matching i2c_master_set_write_dev_addr()'s comment: "write
269:    * slave_addr first, then enable start bit, otherwise the slave_addr
270:    * written will be zero." */
271:   putreg32((uint32_t)(i2c_addr << 1) & BK7258_I2C1_DATA_MASK,
272:            BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_DATA);
273:   g_i2c1_state = BK7258_I2C1_STATE_TX_DEV_ADDR;
274:   modifyreg32(BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS, 0, BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_START);
275: 
276:   leave_critical_section(flags);
277: 
278:   /* Bounded wait: 100ms is generous for a 3-byte 100kHz transaction
279:    * (~270us of bus time) plus scheduling jitter, while still failing
280:    * fast if the slave never responds (e.g. wrong wiring) rather than
281:    * hanging board_late_initialize() indefinitely. */
282:   ret = nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible(&g_i2c1_done_sem, MSEC2TICK(100));
283:   if (ret < 0)
284:     {
285:       /* Timed out: the ISR never ran to completion (either the I2C1
286:        * interrupt never fired at all -- e.g. pinmux/clock
287:        * misconfiguration, or a hardware issue independent of ACK/NACK
288:        * -- or it fired but got stuck mid-sequence).  This is a
289:        * distinct failure mode from a clean NACK (which nxsem_post()s
290:        * promptly with g_i2c1_ack_ok=false) and is logged differently
291:        * here so board bring-up logs can tell "the bus electrically
292:        * never responded at all" apart from "the slave was reachable
293:        * and explicitly rejected". */
294:       printf("i2c1: write_reg(addr=0x%02x, reg=0x%02x) timed out "
295:              "waiting for the I2C1 interrupt (int_status=0x%08x, "
296:              "sm_bus_cfg=0x%08x) -- the ISR never completed the "
297:              "transaction\n",
298:              i2c_addr, reg, (unsigned int)getreg32(BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS),
299:              (unsigned int)getreg32(BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_CFG));
300: 
301:       /* Timed out: force the state machine back to idle so the next
302:        * write_reg() call starts clean, and disable+re-enable the
303:        * peripheral to clear any stuck bus condition, matching
304:        * i2c1_isr_common()'s SCL-timeout recovery path
305:        * (i2c_hal_disable() + i2c_hal_enable()). */
306:       g_i2c1_state = BK7258_I2C1_STATE_IDLE;
307:       modifyreg32(BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_CFG, BK7258_I2C1_CFG_EN, 0);
308:       modifyreg32(BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_CFG, 0, BK7258_I2C1_CFG_EN);
309:       return false;
310:     }
311: 
312:   if (!g_i2c1_ack_ok)
313:     {
314:       printf("i2c1: write_reg(addr=0x%02x, reg=0x%02x) got a clean "
315:              "NACK (the I2C1 interrupt fired and completed, but the "
316:              "slave never pulled ACK) -- the bus is electrically "
317:              "responsive, the device at this address is not\n",
318:              i2c_addr, reg);
319:     }
